x (int): value
y (int): value
Returns:
int: value
"""
return
x
+
y
result
=
tester
(
multiply
)
print
(
result
)
# {'reasoning': "The function's docstring states that it should multiply x by y.
#   However, the implementation returns x + y, which is addition instead of multiplication.
#   Therefore, the implementation does not correctly fulfill what is described in the docstring.",
# 'passed': False}
Basically, we have a
multiply
function that we want to test. To do so we create a
tester
instance that will use
o3-mini
as a judge. Then, we pass the method
multiply
to the
tester
, which internally will build a prompt containing all the information about it. Finally, the LLM will decide if the method is correctly implemented or contains a bug.
How does it work?
I’ve had this project on my todo list for a long time and I never had enough time and motivation to start it, however, some weeks ago
Vincent
released
smartfunc
(a library to turn docstrings into LLM-functions), and motivated me to start the project -and to be honest I borrowed some design choices from Vincent’s code. I also used
llm

Simon Willison
to access different LLM providers easily.
The

Receives a callable
func
as input.
Reads
func
implementation and docstring (using
inspect
library).
Analyzes the implementation of
func
to identify and extract any functions or methods that it calls internally.
Recursively applies steps 1, 2 and 3 to
func
inner methods (up to some
max_depth
).
Builds a
FunctionInfo
object with all the information about
func
we need.
Uses

• **LLM用于文档和代码比对的潜力与风险**：[lgiordano_notte] 认为LLM可以通过比对文档字符串和代码来发现问题，但需要小心过度依赖不充分的文档。
• **LLM代码审查而非测试**：[dragonwriter] 指出，LLM更多是用于代码审查，而非测试。将其称为测试是误导性的。
• **静态类型语言与动态类型语言的比较**：[jonathanlydall] 认为在静态类型语言中，很多验证工作在编译时完成，而在动态类型语言中则需要额外的测试，这可能使得LLM工具在动态类型语言中更有用。
• **AI辅助代码审查而非单元测试**：[jmull] 认为将LLM用于代码审查更合适，而不是单元测试。即使可以自动化运行测试，也需要手动审查结果。
• **LLM作为linter工具的潜力**：[brap] 认为LLM更适合作为linter规则，提供100%覆盖率，但需要选择性使用。

补充讨论：
• **LLM工具的有效性分析**：[yuliyp] 指出需要对LLM工具的有效性进行分析，包括其在实际代码库中的应用效果、误报率和漏报率。
• **代码正确性的证明与尝试**：[evanb] 引用Donald Knuth的话提醒大家，即使代码被证明正确，仍需实际尝试。
• **LLM在代码语义比对和安全审查中的应用**：[JanSchu] 分享了使用LLM进行语义比对的经验，包括其在发现代码与文档不一致、安全风险和不安全调用方面的潜力，同时提醒注意模型提示的压力和错误信心问题。
• **LLM与传统测试方法的比较**：[masklinn] 认为LLM更像是“气氛审查”，而不是证明代码正确性的工具，传统测试方法如属性测试和符号执行仍然不可或缺。
• **LLM在函数式编程中的潜力**：[simianwords] 提出LLM可能在纯函数式编程中更有用，因其无副作用和明确参数传递的特性。
• **LLM测试的随机性问题**：[rollulus] 担心LLM的随机性可能导致测试结果的不稳定。
• **LLM用于文档验证的潜力**：[cerpins] 认为LLM可能适合用于验证文档与代码的一致性，而不需要在代码和文档未改变时重新运行测试。

争议焦点：
• LLM在代码验证和测试中的角色和有效性：一方认为LLM可以有效辅助代码审查和文档比对，另一方则担心其不确定性和潜在误报问题。
• LLM工具的实际应用效果和覆盖率：对LLM工具在实际代码库中的应用效果和误报率、漏报率的分析需求。

总结：讨论围绕LLM在软件开发中的应用展开，主要争议点在于其验证代码的有效性和不确定性问题，同时对其在文档比对和代码审查中的潜力给予了一定认可。

data.article_summary: 本文由Fabien Sanglard撰写，探讨了学习编程语言与掌握编译工具之间的差距。作者回顾了自己学习C和C++语言的愉快经历，得益于许多优秀的教材。然而，学习如何将代码转化为可执行文件的过程却充满挑战，缺乏相关文献。大多数编程书籍仅介绍“Hello World”示例，而未深入讲解编译器使用。本文系列旨在填补这一空白，不教授语言或编写编译器，而是解释如何超越单文件示例，理解可执行文件的创建过程。内容涵盖编译器驱动、预处理、编译、链接和加载五个部分，通过具体步骤和工具帮助读者构建知识体系。本文例子基于Linux平台，但概念适用于其他操作系统。

43891398.article_content:
Driving Compilers
By
Fabien Sanglard
May 3rd, 2023
Mistake - Suggestion
Feedback
Introduction
←
→
I remember how pleasant it was to learn to program in C. There were so many good books explaining not only the language but also the standard library. I devoured both
The C Programming Language (K&R)
by Kernighan/Ritchie and
The Standard C Library
by P.J. Plauger. Then came
Expert C Programming
by Van der Linden and finally
C: A Reference Manual
by Harbison and Steele.
It was an equally enjoyable experience when I took on C++. I found myself unable to put down the
Effective C++
series by Scott Meyers. I loved the simple layout and the astute usage of red text for emphasis. I must have read half the first volume while standing in
Toronto World's Biggest Bookstore
before I left with the complete series under my arm. I remember power walking to my place to keep on reading.
A contrasting experience was to learn how to use the tools to turn my programs into executable. It was a painfully slow and deeply unpleasant process where knowledge was gathered here and there after trial, errors, and a lot of time spent on search engines. It felt like acquiring the same level of comfort to use a compiler took significantly more than learning the language.
I blame this experience on the lack of literature on the topic. Most language books start with a "Hello World" code sample. In the case of K&R, it would be
hello.c
.
#include <stdio.h>
int main()
{
printf("hello, world\n");
}
The reader is given the command to convert that text file into an executable and it is the last time they will hear about how to use the compiler.
$
cc hello.c
$
./a.out
hello, world
This is the gap this series attempts to fill. It won't teach about a language, its libraries, or an SDK. It won't teach how to write a compiler or a linker either. These articles are meant to ease leaving the world of one-file examples. It is a pot-pourri of the things I wish I had known when I was pulling my hair over mysterious
LNK2019
and other
LNK4002
errors.
Here will be explained the core concepts associated with the creation of an executable. As much as possible claims will be backed up with reproducible steps relying on
bintools
and driver verbose mode (
-v
). The goal is to provide the readers with both the tools and a mental map to explore beyond the charted territories of these pages.
Note:
Some liberties were taken with command invocation outputs for typesetting purposes. Commands such as
clang -v
generate a lot more than what is actually printed here. The uninteresting parts were removed to only keep what is relevant to the topic at hand. Rest assured that no command-line tools were hurt during the making of this text.
Environment
The examples assume a Linux platform. Depending on which illustrate the topic better,
gcc
or
clang
compiler drivers are used. If you are using Mac OS X or Windows, the ideas and concepts should be similar. Here is a table of equivalencies.
Platform
Driver
Object format
Dynamic library
Static library
Executable
Linux
gcc
elf
library.so
library.a
elf
Mac OS X
clang
macho
library.dylib
library.a
macho
Windows
CL.EXE
COFF
library.dll
library.lib
PE
The platform / toolchain association is the one most often encountered but they may vary. For example,
clang
is available on all platforms and
gcc
is available on Windows via cygwin.
Structure
1. driver
2. cpp
3. cc
4. ld
5. loader
This series is divided into five parts. First is explained the component which rules them all, the compiler driver
(1)
. Then we drill into the three stages of the compilation pipeline, detailing their inputs/outputs. The pre-processor
(2)
,
cpp
, converts source code files into translation units (TU), is covered first. Then comes the compiler
cc
(3)
, which ingests TUs and outputs relocatable (object) files. Then we look at the element combining all objects together into and executable, the linker
ld
(4)
.
In the fifth and final part we take a look at the linux loader (also called
ld
)
(5)
to further understand the linker output.
Next
The Compiler Driver (1/5)
*

data.title: Unparalleled Misalignments
data.author: ChadNauseam
data.article_summary: 这篇文章列出了一系列“无与伦比的不对齐”（Unparalleled Misalignments），即每对短语中的单词互为同义词，但整个短语的含义不同。例如，“Butt dial”和“Booty call”等。该列表自2018年起由Brian Smiley维护，并接受他人投稿。示例包括：“Home schooled”和“House trained”，“Manual labor”和“Hand job”等。这些短语通过幽默和文字游戏展示了语言的复杂性和多义性。列表中还标注了部分短语的贡献者。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕双关语列表的复杂性、趣味性以及对非母语者的理解难度展开的讨论。

不同观点：
• ben_w分享了自己学习德语的亲身经历，强调成年人学习第二语言的困难，并通过自己误用词语的例子展示了双关语可能带来的尴尬。
• myflash13认为应该为非母语者以及技术术语编写注释，并建议利用ChatGPT来完成这项工作，甚至提出可以构建一个社交网络来评选最佳注释。
• flufluflufluffy以幽默的方式表达了对某些双关语的喜爱，并提议 lesser known rapper 可以以此创作。
• roenxi推测某些双关语可能是诗人故意绕过审查而创作的，将其与编程比赛中的隐藏含义相比较。
• PeterStuer建议将Cockney Slang加入双关语列表，增加趣味性。
• gwern从技术角度提出，可以利用机器学习自动化识别双关语，并讨论了具体的技术实现方法。
• svat欣赏双关语列表的趣味性和巧妙设计，并指出列表的更新活跃。
• 01HNNWZ0MV43FF为“Home-schooled / house trained”提供了详细的解释，帮助非母语者理解。
• saagarjha承认有些双关语需要时间才能理解。
• krisoft认为有些双关语很自然，但有些则显得牵强，比如“fashion”和“taylor”以及“fusion”和“cat”的配对。
• investa和chabska讨论了双关语中“synonyms”的定义，认为这些词语更像是“概念上相邻”而非真正的同义词。
• throw100提出可以寻找在不同语言中有不同定义的较长单词，以此来增加语言学习的趣味性。
• jl6以幽默方式回应了myflash13的评论，提出了“Hacker News / Tweaker Buzz”的配对。

补充讨论：
讨论中涉及到双关语的理解难度、技术实现的可能性以及对某些双关语是否自然的争议。争议的焦点在于双关语的牵强与自然性，以及“synonyms”在这一特定语境下的定义和应用。此外，还涉及到如何帮助非母语者更好地理解这些双关语，以及通过技术手段自动化识别和生成双关语的可能性。

data.title: Towards the Cutest Neural Network
data.author: surprisetalk
data.article_summary:
文章主要讲述了作者尝试在微控制器上使用神经网络来估算物体姿态的过程。由于传感器读数是非线性且相互耦合的，无法通过解析方法解决，作者决定使用简单的神经网络进行近似。具体步骤包括：通过正向模拟生成训练数据，训练一个小型神经网络来学习从传感器读数到姿态的映射，并将该网络部署到微控制器上进行推理。

作者遇到了几个挑战，尤其是在微控制器上进行整数运算推理，因为该设备不支持浮点运算。尽管发现了许多关于“量化”的文献，但大多数库和工具都过于复杂且依赖浮点运算。最终，作者使用了TensorFlow进行量化感知训练，并使用Rust的microflow-rs库进行推理，但仍需解决浮点运算问题以实现纯整数运算。

文章总结了神经网络的基本原理，强调了量化的概念，并希望找到更简洁的解决方案。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：在嵌入式系统上实现小型神经网络的最佳方法，包括训练、量化、推理和代码实现等方面的讨论。

不同观点：
• [gwern] 认为在特定硬件上训练小型整数神经网络时，随机搜索或进化算法（如CMA-ES）是简单有效的方法，因为这些方法易于理解和实现，且不需要外部库。
• [JanSchu] 分享了在Cortex-M0和M3板上进行传感器融合的经验，建议使用固定点运算和CMSIS-NN库来避免浮点运算，并详细描述了从PyTorch原型到C代码实现的工作流程。
• [QuadmasterXLII] 支持JanSchu的观点，并提到使用C++和Eigen进行推理，以及从Python生成C++代码的方法。
• [jasonjmcghee] 提出考虑使用贝叶斯状态估计器，如无迹卡尔曼滤波器，作为另一种方法。
• [mattdesl] 讨论了BitNet（三值权重）在受限硬件上的潜力，并提到固定点运算的精度和性能问题，建议根据具体需求选择浮点或固定点表示。
• [imtringued] 批评原文作者在没有特殊情况下选择原生训练量化神经网络，认为这是不必要的复杂化，并建议使用固定点量化感知训练（QAT）和现有框架。
• [light_hue_1] 认为原文作者在没有系统学习和实验的情况下尝试复杂的方法是错误的，建议从PyTorch等现有框架开始，逐步优化网络和实现。

补充讨论：
• 一些评论提到了具体的工具和资源，如"A Neural Network in 11 lines of Python"教程和BitNet论文及其实现。
• 对于量化方法，有讨论提到训练后静态量化和量化感知训练（QAT）的区别和适用场景。
• 关于硬件优化，有评论提到需要注意指令生成、对齐和填充等问题，以提高性能。
• 对于不同神经网络架构的适用性，有评论提到梯度提升树在某些问题上的优越性能。

争议焦点：
• 是否应该使用现有框架（如PyTorch、TensorFlow）还是手动实现量化神经网络。
• 量化神经网络的训练方法和数据需求，特别是QAT是否需要大量数据。
• 在嵌入式系统上实现神经网络时，选择浮点还是固定点运算的性能和精度权衡。

Towards the cutest neural network ← Back to Kevin's homepage Published: 2025 April 28 I recently needed to use a microcontroller to estimate the pose (translation and orientation) of an object using readings from six different sensors. Since the readings were non-linear and coupled with each other, an explicit analytical solution was out of the question. I figured I’d have a go at using a simple neural network to approximate it: generate training data (on my computer) using a forward simulation (pose to sensor readings) train a lil’ neural network (a few dense layers, 100’s of parameters, tops) to approximate the inverse mapping function (sensor readings to pose) deploy this network on my microcontroller (Cortex-M0, 16 kB RAM, 32 kB flash) to actually do the inference Since neural networks have been around since the 1980’s, I figured it’d be straightforward. A quick background search uncovered lots of promising leads too, especially regarding “quantization”, which I wanted to do as my microcontroller doesn’t have hardware support for floating point operations. However, this turned out to be much more difficult than I’d anticipated. It seems like my use case — end-to-end training of a simple dense neural network with integer-only inference — is quite uncommon. The vast majority of papers and software libraries I found turned out to be complex, heavyweight (in terms of inference code size), and have lots of unstated assumptions and background requirements. To make a web design analogy: It felt like I kept falling into npm create-react-app rabbit holes rather than what I wanted: The moral equivalent of opening index.html with notepad.exe and typing

Welcome to my Homepage

. I’m writing up my notes to: checkpoint my understanding of the space and current best solution help anyone else who simply wants a wholesome lil’ universal function approximator with low conceptual and hardware overhead solicit “why don’t you just …” emails from experienced practitioners who can point me to the library/tutorial I’ve been missing =D (see the alternatives-considered down the page for what I struck out on) tl;dr, how to do it? use TensorFlow to do quantization-aware training and save the resulting model out to a .tflite flatbuffer file use the microflow-rs crate for inference — it’s basically a proc macro that reads tflite file and generates straightforward Rust code that uses nalgebra to multiply matrices Props to Matteo for being seemingly the only person in this space who can put a clear “hello world” inference example in their README.md: use microflow :: model ; #[model( "path/to/model.tflite" )] struct MyModel ; fn main () { let prediction = MyModel :: predict ( input_data ); } It should be cuter. Unfortunately, MicroFlow (and TensorFlow’s out-of-the-box quantization routines, from what I can tell) require floating point operations for inference. While I could use software floating point, I want to make the cutest possible neural network, which means integer arithmetic operations only. (The code size and speed of software floating point depends on the routines used. qfplib-m0-full has a good overview and shows that, e.g., the GCC compiler software floating point multiplication takes 166 cycles.) On the MicroFlow side, removing floating point operations would require a big redesign, as: they’re baked into the API ( predict assumes f32 inputs and outputs). the internals themselves rely on floating point the MicroFlow proc macro reads the .tflite flatbuffer ( source ) when reading a fully-connected layer it combines the various quantization scale factors and zero points into f32 constants these constants are then used during inference at runtime On the TensorFlow side, I can’t find any documentation/options about whether the quantization-aware training routines use floating point activation scaling or if they can model quantized multipliers. But I’m getting ahead of myself — let’s first review the mathematics of neural networks and meaning of “quantization”. The equations require: free parameters $W$ and $b$ (the “weights” and “biases”, respectively); in our case these are a matrix and vector rather than scalar values, since our input data $x$ comes from multiple sensors and the the output pose $y$ has six components (three spatial positions and three spatial rotations) $\sigma$, some nonlinear “activation” function (traditio

“A watch is not a mere tool to tell the time” Casio aimed to put games machines on our wrists
Photograph: Richard Sheppard/Stockimo/Alamy
View image in fullscreen
“A watch is not a mere tool to tell the time” Casio aimed to put games machines on our wrists
Photograph: Richard Sheppard/Stockimo/Alamy
Games
Space Invaders on your wrist: the glory years of Casio video game watches
Their tech may have been primitive, but for 80s schoolchildren of a certain kind they had a glamour to equal any modern iPhone
Keith Stuart
Fri 2 May 2025 04.00 EDT
Last modified on Fri 2 May 2025 23.43 EDT
Share
O
ver the last couple of weeks I have been tidying our attic, and while the general aim has been to prevent its contents from collapsing through the ceiling, I have a side-mission. My most valued possession when I was twelve was a Casio GD-8 Car Race watch – a digital timepiece that included a built-in racing game on its tiny monochrome LCD display. Two big buttons on the front let you steer left and right to avoid incoming vehicles and your aim was to stay alive as long as possible. I lost count of the number of times it was confiscated by teachers at my school. I used to lend it to the hardest boys in the year, thereby guaranteeing me protection against bullies. As a socially inept nerd, this was invaluable to my survival. I’m pretty sure I still have the watch somewhere, and my determination to find it has been augmented by a recent discovery: these things are valuable now.
Casio started making digital watches in the mid-1970s, using technology it had developed in the calculator market to compete on price, but as the decade drew to a close, the market became saturated and the company started to explore new ways to entice buyers.
Speaking to Polygon in 2015
, Yuichi Masuda, senior executive managing officer and Casio board member, explained, “Casio went back to its original thinking when it first entered the watch market; that is, ‘a watch is not a mere tool to tell the time.’ We started talking about a multifunction [approach], time display plus other things, such as telephone number memory and music alarms.”
View image in fullscreen
Taking off … children playing Space Invaders in 1980.
Photograph: Eugene Adebari/REX/Shutterstock
At the time, Taito’s arcade game Space Invaders was a phenomenon in Japan. And so in 1981 Casio launched the CA-90/CA-901, a chunky calculator watch that included a sort of space shoot-’em-up but with numbers rather than alien spaceships advancing down the screen. “We wanted to create a new lifestyle of enjoying the game anywhere at any time,” said Masuda.
But wasn’t Casio also inspired by Nintendo’s Game & Watch series? After all, this iconic range of handheld electronic games started in 1980 with the juggling and catching sim Ball, and its success led to a vast array of titles, including the famed two-screen Donkey Kong that inspired the Nintendo DS. Shinji Saito, general manager and chief producer at the product planning department of Casio’s timepiece business unit, says not. “In 1980, the year before Casio launched the CA-90, Casio launched the MG-880, a game calculator that allowed users to enjoy digital invaders. Nintendo’s Game & Watch was also launched in 1980,” he says. “In developing the CA-90, Casio utilised the development assets of its MG-880 game calculator, but the starting point for the idea was Casio’s development philosophy of creating a new culture using light, thin, short and low-power technology. We were
not
inspired by Nintendo’s Game & Watch.”
Indeed, Casio was developing a wide array of innovative features at the time including databanks, thermometers and pulse checkers. “Their entire watch range in the 80s was huge,” says watch enthusiast Andy Bagley. “I have been collecting for years and even now I will still come across a model I haven’t seen before; there were many hundreds. I only recently discovered Casio made a range of touch screen watches in the 80s – way ahead of their time!”

data.title: Apple Shortcuts is falling into "the automation gap"
data.author: walterbell
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了Mac上Shortcuts功能的进展缓慢问题。作者John Voorhees回顾了三年前对AppleScript通过Shortcuts集成的质疑，指出如果Shortcuts要成为Mac上自动化任务的主要方式，需要每年稳步进展。然而，Shortcuts在Mac上的发展并不稳定，作者通过复杂的多工具自动化实例（如Stream Deck、Keyboard Maestro、JavaScript、AppleScript等）展示了目前Shortcuts的不足。尽管Apple希望通过App Intents改进Shortcuts，但其功能仍显不足，尤其是在条件语句等方面。作者认为，Apple宣称的“多年过程”已过去近四年，改进空间有限。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Apple的Shortcuts应用的功能、限制及其在自动化中的作用。

不同观点：
• [jtrn] 认为Shortcuts功能受限，尤其是无法使用如粘贴、按键或SMS作为触发器，认为这些限制并非技术原因，而是Apple的哲学或政治考量。
• [rcarmo] 指出Shortcuts在iOS上勉强可用，在macOS上几乎无用，因为有Automator和AppleScript等更强大的工具，但这些工具随着时间推移被苹果忽视。
• [walterbell] 提供了多个利用Shortcuts实现复杂功能的实例，如通过SSH脚本运行外部任务、使用URL方案驱动特定应用，以及通过物理接近触发快捷指令，展示了Shortcuts的潜力。
• [DidYaWipe] 对Apple能否创建全面的系统级脚本持怀疑态度，认为Apple应先改善其日益糟糕的框架。
• [hn_throw2025] 对Shortcuts持积极态度，分享了如何将其用于家庭自动化，如通过SSH控制家庭媒体中心和智能开关。
• [dawnerd] 希望Shortcuts能实现简单的自动化，如在进入车内时自动打开热点，但对其可靠性表示失望。
• [jbverschoor] 认为Shortcuts对程序员和非程序员都不友好，因为它没有明确的目标用户。
• [nunez] 认为Shortcuts既有极大的用处又极其令人沮丧，因为其功能有时会因iOS更新而失效，且错误处理不佳。
• [aucisson_masque] 认为Shortcuts是iPhone相较于Android的一大卖点，但其复杂性使得普通用户不会使用，Apple可能不会优先考虑其改进。
• [hirvi74] 更喜欢使用AppleScript和Swift进行自动化，但仍欣赏Shortcuts可以通过CLI调用的特性。
• [jfernandezr] 仅使用Shortcuts记录工作里程，认为其集成的应用不足。
• [impish9208] 利用Shortcuts实现VPN的自动连接和断开，但对每次运行时生成锁屏通知无法关闭表示不满。
• [undebuggable] 对Shortcuts的文档和功能不足表示失望，曾经有效的功能因iOS更新而失效。
• [oneeyedpigeon] 认为Shortcuts在macOS上是一个不错的应用，但相较于Automator仍显不足。
• [sholladay] 分享了创建“门开太久”警报时的多种问题，包括个人快捷指令和家庭快捷指令的不一致、音量控制问题等，对Shortcuts的功能限制表达了不满。

补充讨论：
• Shortcuts的功能和限制引发了关于Apple在自动化工具方面的哲学和优先级的广泛讨论。
• 用户对Shortcuts的期望和实际体验之间存在差距，尤其是在可靠性和功能性方面。
• 不同用户根据自身需求对Shortcuts的评价各异，有些用户找到创造性的解决方案，而有些用户则感到挫败。
• 对Apple能否改善Shortcuts及其框架的怀疑态度，以及对更强大、更可靠自动化工具的渴望。

43892481.article_content:
MENU
This Week's Sponsor
Magic Lasso Adblock
:
2.0x faster web browsing in Safari
by Jason Snell
March 28, 2025 1:46 PM
PT
Shortcuts is falling into “the automation gap”
John Voorhees,
writing on Club MacStories
(subscription required):
Nearly three years ago, I wrote
AppleScript: Shortcuts Bridge or Crutch?
, questioning whether accessing AppleScript via Shortcuts on the Mac was a feature to be celebrated or a red flag, fearing that Apple would use the integration to postpone or never release many of the system-level actions that were missing from Shortcuts’ debut on the Mac.
As I put it then, “if Shortcuts is to become the default way to automate tasks on the Mac, there needs to be steady, yearly progress to make macOS and its default system apps as Shortcuts-friendly as possible. There’s a role for AppleScript to play in Shortcuts that won’t go away anytime soon, but not as a way to fill the potholes left by missing Shortcuts actions.”
Shortcuts’ progress on the Mac has been anything but steady and yearly.
A few days ago, while writing my
Podcast Notes update
, I realized that I had (inadvertently?) created an automation that begins with a Stream Deck keypress that executes a Keyboard Maestro macro that kicks off a JavaScript script in Audio Hijack that runs an AppleScript applet that executes a Shortcuts shortcut. In recent days I’ve also edited shortcuts that run Python and AppleScript scripts, including some where the shortcut is really nothing more than a Mac UI-friendly wrapper around a bare script, much in the same way you can use Automator as a simple wrapper around AppleScript scripts.
That all these things are possible on the Mac is amazing, and it’s a testament to how flexible and powerful the Mac can be. But it also says something quite profound about how little progress Apple has made with Shortcuts on the Mac (or in general) in the last few years. (And of course, all these workarounds fail on iOS entirely.)
Maybe the drive toward App Intents will help make Shortcuts more powerful and less reliant on tools like AppleScript, Keyboard Maestro, and the rest. But even that isn’t enough, since the Shortcuts app is way too rickety and limited. Just the other day, Dan Moren said to me, “I was working on a shortcut and I needed an if-else-if statement,” and we both began laughing because conditionals are just
so bad
in Shortcuts.
Apple gave itself a lot of leeway by declaring that Shortcuts was the “beginning of a years-long process” to make Shortcuts the “future of automation on the Mac.” But that was almost four years ago. There’s not a lot of leeway left for me to give.

data.title: Visualising home sun exposure with Rhino
data.author: ostwilkens
data.article_summary: 本文是一位屋主对房屋日照情况的回顾和可视化过程的分享，而非指导指南。作者在房屋 renovation 时意识到日照对不同区域的重要性，尤其是避免在缺乏日照的阳台浪费资金。为了更好地理解日照情况，作者使用Rhino 3D软件及其插件Grasshopper和Ladybug进行了日照模拟。通过这些模拟，作者发现早晨地面阴影处适合户外早餐，院子和可接近的较低屋顶适合午餐，而西向阳台由于日照不足不适合晚餐。最终，作者决定取消对西阳台的原计划，从而节省开支。此外，通过模拟发现屋顶仍适合安装太阳能板，未来可能会考虑使用太阳能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：DIY太阳能项目工具和应用的比较

不同观点：
• [xnx] 认为该项目类似于Google的"Project Sunroof"工具，并分享了相关链接（https://sunroof.withgoogle.com/），强调其作为DIY项目的潜力。
• [dmos62] 对[xnx]提到的工具表示赞赏，认为它比想象中更简单，同时提出了另一个工具"Sun Surveyor"（https://www.sunsurveyor.com/），该工具可以通过3D可视化和实时摄像头覆盖功能（LiveView）帮助用户在任何时间和年份查看太阳的位置。dmos62个人非常喜欢这个应用，尽管使用频率不高。

补充讨论：
• [dmos62] 提供了对"Sun Surveyor"应用的具体使用体验，特别是其独特的LiveView功能，这为类似项目提供了另一种选择和实用工具。
• 争议的焦点可能在于用户对工具的选择偏好，具体取决于项目的需求和对功能的要求。例如，Google的Project Sunroof可能更适合太阳能项目的初步评估，而Sun Surveyor则提供了更详细的实时数据和3D可视化功能。

总结：讨论主要围绕两种工具的比较展开，参与者分享了各自的使用经验和偏好，提供了对DIY太阳能项目有用的不同工具选项。

43856208.article_content:
Visualising sun exposure for our house
Disclaimer: this is not a guide, but a retrospective surface-level documentation of what I achieved
We're doing a lot of renovations right now. I've been thinking about how our house is used, but also how it could change in the future. One thing I didn't give much thought when initially looking at the house is how it relates to the cardinal directions. Well, we've been living here 4 years now, and I'm just now realizing we don't have a lot of evening sun.
When considering how much attention and money to allocate to different areas, I realized sun exposure is really important. I don't want to spend tons of money on a balcony that never sees the sun. And so I thought, this must be possible to visualize with software.
My conversation on TypingMind
I had no idea where to begin, so I asked ChatGPT. It suggested trying the following:
Sketchup with extensions
Rhino with Ladybug
Autodesk Revit
Going with Rhino 3D
Rhino has a month-long trial version which works on MacOS, and also seemed powerful enough to do what I want.
It took some getting used to, searching the documentation, and following youtube tutorials. But after (quite) a few hours, I had a somewhat precise model of my building and the surrounding area. I utilized old drawings of our house, and made some measurements by hand. Working with Rhino feels like a very peculiar mix of CAD and 3d modeling software like Blender.
Bear with me, there are some names to keep track of.
Rhino is the main software.
Grasshopper is a visual programming interface (with a Python backend)
Ladybug is an extension to Grasshopper, which allows for sun calculations.
There are some great tutorials for Ladybug on youtube, which will help you achieve the same things as me.
Simulation results
I wanted to determine which areas are fitting for a nice summer lunch, or dinner. I ran the following simulations:
The sun is intense in the morning. Most likely, if we're looking for a nice outdoor breakfast, we'll do it in a shade on the ground level.
It looks like the yard on ground level is a good fit for lunch as well. The lower roof would also be a good fit, if we were to make it accessible.
As suspected, evening sun is looking grim. What I learned is: if we plan in advance, we can get a few hours of sun for a nice dinner on our west-facing balcony.
Main takeaway: We had some plans for the west balcony. Seeing as it doesn't get much sun at all, we're scrapping those plans, and just doing the minimum. Money saved!
Solar surprise
A bonus simulation: Incident Radiation. Because we barely experience the sun from the south, I expected solar panels to be a bad pick for us. Turns out, our roof actually has a different experience! Seeing this, we might actually consider solar energy in the future.

data.title: AWS Built a Security Tool. It Introduced a Security Risk
data.author: simplesort
data.article_summary: 这篇文章讨论了AWS的一个安全工具“Account Assessment for AWS Organizations”意外引入了跨账户权限提升的风险。该工具旨在审核基于资源的跨账户访问，但由于部署指南不够明确，导致用户在不安全的账户中部署，从而造成安全隐患。具体来说，AWS建议将枢纽角色部署在除管理账户外的任何账户中，这可能让低安全性的账户获得对高敏感账户的访问权限。这种配置可能被攻击者利用，通过开发账户中的角色获取生产和管理工作中的敏感数据和权限。AWS之后修复了该问题，并建议受影响的组织检测和修复不安全的配置。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：AWS环境中的安全风险及其处理方式

不同观点：
• **yfiapo**：认为这是一个已经适当处理的中等严重性安全问题。信息披露本身并不能被直接利用，只有在攻击者已经获得一定访问权限的情况下才可能被滥用。AWS的文档只是没有明确指出最佳实践，而不是推荐不安全的设置。过度夸大这样的小问题对任何人都没有帮助。

• **placardloop**：不认为这是安全问题。List* API仅提供元数据，不包含实际对象，因此无法直接构成安全威胁。如果秘密信息被存储在桶名称中，那属于更大的问题。

• **18172828286177**：认为是部署人员的 incompetence 导致的，而不是AWS的问题。AWS已经警告过不要在管理账户中部署，但部署人员未遵守。

• **abhisek**：IAM系统本身非常复杂，尤其是在联合和跨账户信任的情况下。并非每个弱点都可以被视为漏洞，需要明确的威胁模型来评估。

• **dangus**：从AWS转到Google Cloud的体验出发，指出GCP的账户和资源管理更加灵活和安全，认为AWS需要进行重大改革。

• **MikeIndyson**：强调不应该在元数据中存储敏感数据，这是实施上的问题而不是AWS本身的缺陷。

• **atoav**：通过比喻说明许多安全解决方案的问题在于给予某些部分过多的权限，一旦这些部分被攻破，整个系统就会面临风险。强调严格的分区和持续的审查是安全的关键。

• **swisniewski**：强烈反对文章的观点，认为AWS的模型已经很清晰，跨账户访问需要显式配置。文章夸大了问题，实际上只是工程师部署时的错误，而非AWS的安全风险。

补充讨论：
• **bulatb**和**gitroom**：对文章的简短标题和过度担忧表达了不满和反思，认为不同人对风险的看法和界定标准不同。

• **tasuki**和**ahoka**：对整个安全行业和工具持怀疑态度，认为许多安全工具本身就可能引入风险，甚至安全套件本身也会造成不便（如封锁链接）。

争议焦点：
• 这个问题的严重性和是否应被视为安全漏洞是主要争议点。一部分人认为这只是实施问题或小范围的风险，而另一部分人则认为即使是元数据披露也值得关注。

• 另一个争议点是AWS是否应在其文档中更明确地指出最佳实践，还是应由用户自行确保其部署环境的安全性。

43893906.article_content:
Blog
Apr 28, 2025 | 7 min
AWS Built a Security Tool. It Introduced a Security Risk.
Eliav Livneh
Security Researcher
(If you missed the previous parts of this trust policy blog series, we recommend reading parts
one
and
two
first)
In the previous post of this series, we explored four dangerous misconceptions regarding how to securely set up cross-account access in AWS environments.
In this final post of the series, weâll walk through a real-world case where even AWS got it wrong. Their
Account Assessment for AWS Organizations
tool, designed to audit resource-based policies for risky cross-account access, ironically introduced cross-account privilege escalation risks due to flawed deployment instructions. Specifically, customers were effectively encouraged to deploy the tool in lower-sensitivity accounts, creating risky trust paths from insecure environments into highly sensitive ones.
Weâll share how we discovered the issue, the risks it introduced, how AWS fixed it, and what affected organizations should do to detect and remediate it.
How it started
While investigating a critical privilege escalation risk involving an IAM role in a customerâs AWS environment, we discovered a role present in both their production and management accounts, each of which trusted two roles in their development account:
The risky IAM role we investigated
These were the details of the privilege escalation risk (sensitive info redacted):
Examining the permissions of that role in the production and management accounts, we found it had access to several sensitive IAM and data-related API calls, including:
iam:ListRoles
(lists all IAM roles, helping an attacker identify privileged and vulnerable roles)
iam:ListPolicies
(reveals all IAM policies, exposing potential misconfigurations)
secretsmanager:ListSecrets
(lists all stored secret names, identifying potential targets)
s3:ListAllMyBuckets
(enumerates all S3 buckets, exposing potential sensitive data locations)
kms:ListKeys
(lists all encryption keys, indicating what is being encrypted)
kms:GetKeyPolicy
(retrieves key policies, which could reveal weak or misconfigured access controls)
â¦ and more (full policy
here
)
These permissions were granted on all resources (
resource: "*"
), making them particularly dangerous if compromised.
The organization's dev account had weaker security, making this role assumption path a major risk. An attacker compromising a trusted role in dev could immediately gain these permissions in production and management. Combined with other misconfigurations - such as exposed IAM roles, secret names, KMS keys, or public S3 buckets - this could help lead to compromise of the organization's most sensitive accounts.
This was already a serious risk, but what we found next revealed that this misconfiguration was not unique to this organization - it was actually inadvertently encouraged by AWS itself.
Account Assessment for AWS Organizations
The names of these roles were somewhat quirky, and hinted they were part of some automated system. A quick search led us to
Account Assessment for AWS Organizations
, a tool developed by AWS and published in the
AWS Solutions Library
.
According to its official documentation, the tool is designed to âcentrally evaluate and manage AWS accounts within your AWS Organizationsâ, helping users better understand account dependencies. AWS lists its
primary use cases
as mergers and acquisitions, security audits, centralized policy explorer and management account transitions.
So, why was it deployed insecurely?
Given that this tool was built by AWS to audit resource-based cross-account access, we initially assumed the misconfiguration was a deployment error by the customer. However, after reviewing the documentation, we realized that AWSâs deployment instructions unintentionally encouraged insecure setups, making it highly likely that users would deploy the tool in a way that introduced privilege escalation risks.
The tool follows a hub-and-spoke architecture:
A hub role is deployed in a designated hub account.
Spoke roles are deployed in all other accounts to be assessed, trusting the hub role for access.
This design allows the hub role to assume the spoke roles across all accounts, aggregating security data across the organization.
When checking AWS's official deployment guidance, we were surprised to see the following instruction:
"Hub stack - Deploy to any member account in your AWS Organization except the Organizations management account."
This is the root cause of the issue - AWS explicitly recommended not deploying the hub in the management account, without clarifying the security implications of the other possible choices.
Why this is a major security risk
Letâs back up a bit and explain why this instruction, without any clarification, was so problematic.
As we covered in the
previous blog
, allowing a role in a less secure account to assume roles in more sensitive accounts creates a privilege escalation risk.
By d

data.title: The vocal effects of Daft Punk
data.author: qzervaas
data.article_summary: Daft Punk广泛使用多种声乐效果器，包括Roland SVC-350、Auto-Tune、DigiTech Vocalist和Talker，以及Sennheiser VSM201等。根据专辑和歌曲的不同，使用的效果器也有所变化。在《Homework》中，主要使用Roland SVC-350和Ensoniq DP/4+进行音高变换。在《Discovery》中，出现了Auto-Tune和DigiTech Vocalist，而《Human After All》则大量使用DigiTech Talker。在《Random Access Memories》中，Sennheiser VSM201成为主要效果器，同时也有Talk Box和Auto-Tune的应用。Daft Punk的声效可以大致分为Talk Box、声码器和和声器三类，每种技术产生不同的机器人声效果。尽管效果相似，但它们基于不同的技术和设备。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：关于一篇深入研究Daft Punk音乐效果的文章及其相关音乐设备的讨论

补充讨论：
• [设备与价格] 用户tecleandor提到Sennheiser VSM201的高价和稀有性，指出虽然可以用更便宜的设备达到类似效果，但高价设备仍有其独特之处。

43893601.article_content:
The vocal effects of Daft Punk
Daft Punk have used a wide variety of vocal effects in their songs. A May 2001 interview in Remix magazine provided a rare insight from Daft Punk themselves on the topic.
âPeople always ask us what vocoder we use, but every one of our vocal tracks uses a different vocoder effect. We have the old Roland one [an SVC-350], Auto-Tune, and a DigiTech Vocalist.â
The quote delivers some vital clues, but itâs incomplete, covering only their first two albums. Thereâs no mention of using a talk box, despite Around The World almost certainly using one. The quote makes it sound like the DigiTech Vocalist is a vocoder, but itâs not. And for that matter, which DigiTech Vocalist model? Thereâs around 30 pieces of hardware in DigiTechâs Vocalist series, and quite a few of them were around before Discoveryâs release in 2001.
Iâve read comments suggesting the DigiTech Vocalist models with the âEXâ suffix are special, but nobody seems to know why, and nobody has published a direct comparison to prove or disprove the theory. I decided to take on the challenge, and run the tests myself. Hereâs a fraction of the Vocalist units I ended up buying.
Why are there duplicates of the same model? Why is there a Korg ih in that photo? Before this article gets sidetracked with tests and some honestly quite interesting corporate partnerships, mergers, and lawsuits, here is a list of every Daft Punk album song containing robot-like vocal effects, and my guess on which piece of kit was used for the vocals.

Homework notes (20 January 1997)
#
There arenât many robot vocal effects on Homework, but there is a lot of pitch shifting, likely provided by Daft Punkâs Ensoniq DP/4+, a digital multi-effects units that can do a variety of things. I donât believe Daft Punk used the vocoder on the Ensoniq DP/4+ for Homework or any of their other albums. The Remix magazine quote says Ensoniq DP/4, but a
gear list in another interview
says DP/4+. It doesnât matter which model was used, as the pitch shifting and vocoder sound the same on both units.
Discovery notes (12 March 2001)
#
One More Time sounds like Auto-Tune in combination with a Mu-Tron Phasor or Moogerfooger. Harder, Better, Faster, Stronger uses a DigiTech Talker vocoder. Given the DigiTech Talker was used extensively for Human After All, maybe it was one of the last songs recorded for Discovery? The DigiTech Talker wasnât mentioned in the May 2001 interview, despite its use on Discovery.
Human After All notes (14 March 2005)
#
DigiTech Talker and DigiTech Synth Wah are all over the entire album. But, did they use a DigiTech Synth Wah, or DigiTech Bass Synth Wah? Theyâre very similar pedals. The tremolo effect on The Brainwasher could have been done many ways. Maybe it was just an LFO modulating the amplitude on their Roland S-760 sampler? Maybe it was a guitar pedal? Itâs an easy effect that can be achieved many different ways.
Random Access Memories notes (17 May 2013)
#
In Lose Yourself To Dance, the âeverybodyâs dancing on the floorâ vocals sound very crunchy and DigiTech Talker-like. The vocodeded vocals in Touch sound like a Sennheiser VSM201 switched to unvoiced, or using white noise as the vocoderâs carrier. Instant Crush could be Auto-Tune or some other kind of harmoniser. It sounds like Instant Crush constains some Sennheiser VSM201 chord layers in places.
Talk boxes
#
Daft Punkâs vocal effects can be broadly split into three categories: Talk boxes, vocoders, and harmonisers. They all sound vaguely similar and robot-like, and you could be forgiven for confusing them, but theyâre extremely different techniques and technologies.

data.article_summary: 2025年5月，唐纳德·特朗普宣布对所有“外国制作”的电影征收100%关税，称外国激励措施导致美国电影业快速衰退，构成“国家安全威胁”和“宣传”。他指示商务部立即实施该关税。此举引发国际反应，澳大利亚和新西兰表示将保护本国电影业。专家警告，此关税可能引发报复，损害美国电影业。此前，特朗普对华发起贸易战，中国已减少美国电影进口配额，进一步影响好莱坞。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：针对“MAGA支持者攻击好莱坞”的评论及相关争议

不同观点：
• **habosa的观点**：认为好莱坞在全球推广美国文化，具有政府无法实现的影响力，威胁好莱坞是愚蠢的行为，因为好莱坞为美国带来了巨大的文化优势。
  
• **jaimebuelta的观点**：质疑好莱坞项目的“美国属性”，指出像《Deadpool & Wolverine》这样的电影主要在英国拍摄，主演也不是美国人，质疑是否要为此类电影支付双倍票价或聚焦国际市场。

• **pluc的观点**：将攻击好莱坞与“美国优先”政策联系起来，认为这是在文化教育领域进行削减，最终目的是通过宣传控制民众思想，且目前没有强有力的反对。

• **mk89的观点**：以讽刺口吻提到如果好莱坞项目转移到美国国内拍摄可能产生的荒谬结果，如在乔治亚州拍摄《罗马》或在大峡谷拍摄《指环王》。

• **d3nj4l的观点**：认为讨论中很多观点没有实质内容，质疑如何对电影征税及其实施细节，认为人们过度解读。

• **Ekaros的观点**：指出对好莱坞征税可能打击美国少数具有贸易顺差的产业之一，认为这样做是不明智的。

• **bilekas的观点**：质疑是否有实际的政策文件或只是集会上的 rant，希望了解对外国电影征税的国家安全理由。

• **xz18r的观点**：指出在美国以外的国家，几乎所有听到的电影都是美国的，质疑反对MAGA的人说“美国从未伟大”的同时，又声称“电影从未离开美国”。

• **victorbjorklund的观点**：认为欧盟政治家可能会利用这个机会支持欧洲电影产业。

• **perihelions的观点**：从法律角度质疑美国是否可以通过宪法第一修正案对媒体征税，并探讨禁止媒体的宪法界限。

• **trebligdivad的观点**：以讽刺口吻预测未来可能要求《Wallace & Gromit》采用美国幽默。

• **drooopy的观点**：以讽刺方式预测未来可能出现更荒谬的政策，如要求用Gatorade浇灌作物。

• **codingbot3000的观点**：关注特朗普在Truth Social上的帖子获得的点赞数很少，质疑为何没有更多的互动。

• **jpambrun的观点**：质疑如何对电影征税，猜测Netflix可能会根据观看量被收费，并预测其他国家会进行报复，导致美国电影制作成本增加和海外被征税，可能引发盗版增加。

• **steveBK123的观点**：以讽刺口吻指出有人可能因为Netflix上太多字幕电影而生气。

补充讨论：
- 讨论中涉及了好莱坞在全球文化传播中的重要性及其经济影响。
- 对电影征税的具体实施细节和法律问题是另一个讨论重点。
- 有人质疑这种政策是否会适得其反，导致美国电影产业受损。
- 讽刺和幽默被广泛用于表达对政策的不满和预测可能出现的荒谬结果。
- 讨论中还涉及了国际市场的反应及可能的经济后果。

43893310.article_content:
1:04
Donald Trump announces tariff on movies from 'other nations'  – video
Donald Trump
Trump announces 100% tariffs on movies ‘produced in foreign lands’
President calls films ‘national security threat’ and claims he called on commerce department to immediately enact tariff
Guardian staff and agencies
Sun 4 May 2025 19.54 EDT
Last modified on Mon 5 May 2025 08.21 EDT
Share
Donald Trump
on Sunday announced on his Truth Social platform a 100%
tariff
on all movies “produced in Foreign Lands”, saying the US film industry was dying a “very fast death” due to the incentives that other countries were offering to draw American film-makers.
In his post, he claimed to have authorised the commerce department and the US trade representative to immediately begin instituting such a tariff.
“This is a concerted effort by other Nations and, therefore, a National Security threat,” Trump said in
the Truth Social post
. “It is, in addition to everything else, messaging and propaganda!
“WE WANT MOVIES MADE IN AMERICA, AGAIN!” Trump added.
Republicans in Congress pull out all the stops to protect Trump tariffs
Read more
The commerce secretary, Howard Lutnick, posting on X said: “We’re on it.” Neither Lutnick nor Trump provided any details on the implementation. It was not immediately clear whether the move would target production companies, foreign or American, producing films overseas.
Film and television production in Los Angeles has fallen by nearly 40% over the last decade, according to FilmLA, a non-profit that tracks the region’s production. At the same time, governments around the world have offered more generous tax credits and cash rebates to lure productions, and capture a greater share of the $248bn that Ampere Analysis predicts will be spent globally in 2025 to produce content.
Politicians in Australia and New Zealand said on Monday they would advocate for their respective film industries, after the president’s announcement.
Australia’s home affairs minister, Tony Burke, said he had spoken to the head of the government body Screen Australia about the proposed tariffs. “Nobody should be under any doubt that we will be standing up unequivocally for the rights of the Australian screen industry,” he said in a statement.
‘It feels empty’: is Hollywood film and TV production in a death spiral?
Read more
New Zealand’s prime minister, Christopher Luxon, told a news conference the government was awaiting further detail of the proposed tariffs. “We’ll have to see the detail of what actually ultimately emerges. But we’ll be obviously a great advocate, great champion of that sector in that industry,” he said.
The announcement from Trump comes after he triggered a trade war with China, and imposed global tariffs which have roiled markets and led to fears of a US recession. The film industry has already been feeling the effects of the tariffs, as China in April responded to the announcements by
reducing the quota
of American movies allowed into that country.
China is the world’s second largest film market after the US, although in recent years domestic offerings have outshone Hollywood imports.
A former senior commerce department official, William Reinsch, a senior fellow with the Center for Strategic and International Studies, said retaliation against Trump’s foreign movies tariffs would be devastating.
“The retaliation will kill our industry. We have a lot more to lose than to gain,” he said, adding that it would be difficult to make a national security or national emergency case for movies.

data.title: Effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation on sleep bruxism
data.author: amelius
data.article_summary: 这篇研究探讨了重复经颅磁刺激（rTMS）对睡眠磨牙症（SB）患者的短期影响。12名SB患者参与了一项开放性、单次干预的试点研究。研究对患者双侧初级运动皮层中的咬肌代表区施加1 Hz、80%活动运动阈值强度的rTMS，每天每侧20分钟，连续5天。使用便携式肌电图（EMG）记录仪测量患者睡眠期间 jaw-closing 肌肉的EMG活动，并通过0-10数字评分量表（NRS）评估肌肉酸痛。结果显示，rTMS期间及之后，EMG活动强度和NRS酸痛评分均显著低于基线水平（P值分别为0.04、0.02和<0.01）。研究表明，rTMS可显著抑制睡眠期间的 jaw-closing 肌肉活动，并减轻肌肉酸痛，提示rTMS对磨牙症具有潜在治疗效果，但需进一步开展更严格的对照研究。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：牙齿磨削（bruxism）的原因、影响及其处理方法

不同观点：
• [noworld] 提供了关于牙齿磨削（bruxism）的医学定义和基本信息，引用了Mayo Clinic的定义，指出磨牙是牙齿挤压或摩擦的情况，可能与情绪或心理状态有关。

• [diob] 分享了个人的经历，表示因为 bruxism 不得不停止服用 sertraline（一种抗抑郁药物），但同时承认该药物对焦虑和情绪有显著帮助，目前正在考虑是否重新服用。这表明了药物治疗效果与副作用之间的权衡。

• [aaroninsf] 提出了一个警告性建议，强调了 bruxism 可能导致的长期健康问题（如根管治疗或拔牙），并建议至少使用护齿器来保护牙齿，表明了对预防性措施的重视。

补充讨论：
• [diob] 的评论引出了药物副作用与心理健康之间的争议，特别是 sertraline 对情绪的帮助与 bruxism 副作用之间的取舍。

• [aaroninsf] 的评论则强调了 bruxism 的潜在严重后果，并提出了实际的防护措施（如佩戴护齿器），指出了及时处理牙齿磨削问题的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 药物治疗（如 sertraline）对心理健康的益处与其可能引发的 bruxism 副作用之间的权衡是讨论中的一个争议点。个人需要在情绪改善与牙齿健康之间做出选择。

• 另一个值得注意的讨论点是如何有效预防和处理 bruxism，以避免长期牙齿损伤，[aaroninsf] 的建议强调了早期干预的重要性。

Abstract
The purpose of this study was to investigate the effects of repetitive transcranial magnetic stimulation (rTMS) on patients with sleep bruxism (SB). Twelve patients with SB were included in an open, single-intervention pilot study. rTMS at 1 Hz and an intensity of 80% of the active motor threshold was applied to the ‘hot spot' of the masseter muscle representation at the primary motor cortex bilaterally for 20 min per side each day for 5 consecutive days. The jaw-closing muscle electromyographic (EMG) activity during sleep was recorded with a portable EMG recorder at baseline, during rTMS treatment and at follow-up for 5 days. In addition, patients scored their jaw-closing muscle soreness on a 0–10 numerical rating scale (NRS). Data were analysed with analysis of variance. The intensity of the EMG activity was suppressed during and after rTMS compared to the baseline (
P
= 0.04;
P
= 0.02, respectively). The NRS score of soreness decreased significantly during and after rTMS compared with baseline (
P
< 0.01). These findings indicated a significant inhibition of jaw-closing muscle activity during sleep along with a decrease of muscle soreness. This pilot study raises the possibility of therapeutic benefits from rTMS in patients with bruxism and calls for further and more controlled studies.
Keywords:
behavioural science, brain function, electromyography, orofacial pain,

data.article_summary: CodeCafé是一个基于浏览器的实时协作代码编辑器，专为高效团队编程设计。它支持多人同时编辑代码，具备像素完美的实时预览功能，并使用Operational Transformation技术解决编辑冲突。编辑器提供类似VS Code的开发体验，包括语法高亮、智能提示和错误检查。前端采用React和TypeScript，后端使用Java Spring Boot，通过WebSocket和Redis实现实时协作。主要功能包括零设置、即刻编码，以及未来计划添加的用户认证、项目持久化、语音/文本聊天等。项目基于AGPL-3.0许可证开源。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：该评论区讨论了一个新发布项目的功能、技术实现以及可能的应用场景，涉及用户体验、技术选型、功能扩展等方面。

不同观点：
• [omneity]  congratulated the release，并建议增加页面加载时自动生成唯一URL的功能，以增强用户体验和操作信心。此外，他还提出了这个工具是否能作为开发者之间协作的更好方式，提出了从“为我写代码”到“与我结对编程”的协作理念。
• [jasonjmcghee] 称赞项目的同时，澄清了在使用该工具时，被分享者（sharee）不需要账户即可在浏览器中使用共享功能，并指出在代码执行方面Replit可能更适合，但其免费层资源有限。
• [tpae] 对项目的技术选型提出疑问，建议使用CDRT（可能指某种技术框架或工具）如yjs，认为这样可以简化代码库。
• [indigodaddy] 关注预览功能是否支持动态服务器内容（如Python、Node.js、PHP等），暗示对该功能适用范围的关心。
• [nanna] 表达了对Emacs版本的期望，显示出对该工具在不同开发环境中的扩展需求。

补充讨论：
• 用户[omneity]和[jasonjmcghee]之间的讨论涉及如何在不同工具之间做选择，尤其是涉及到代码共享与执行功能时，Replit被提及作为对比。
• 技术实现方面，用户[tpae]对使用CDRT如yjs的建议可能引发对当前技术栈的讨论，涉及到简化代码库和开发复杂度的问题。
• 功能扩展方面，用户[indigodaddy]和[nanna]分别关注对不同编程语言和开发环境的支持，显示出对工具灵活性和广泛适用性的需求。

争议焦点：
• 主要集中在技术实现和功能扩展上，例如是否使用CDRT如yjs来简化代码库，以及对动态服务器内容的支持程度。

CodeCafé: Code Together, Instantly.
A hyper-collaborative, real-time development environment right in your browser. CodeCafé makes pair programming, teaching, and building web projects together as fluid and instant as sharing a thought.
Try CodeCafé Live!
Click here to watch the demo video!
Why CodeCafé?
We saw coding classes juggling tools built for essays, not engineers. Existing solutions felt clunky for the dynamic nature of real-time programming. CodeCafé was born from the need for a seamless, browser-based coding space designed from the ground up for
true
collaboration. Learn, teach, and build—together, instantly.
Core Features
Pixel-Perfect Live Preview:
See your HTML, CSS, and JavaScript changes render
instantly
in an integrated Web View. What you code is what you see!
True Real-Time Collaboration:
Powered by Operational Transformation, multiple users can type in the same files simultaneously, with conflicts resolved seamlessly.
VS Code Feel:
Enjoy a familiar, rich editing experience (via Monaco Editor) with syntax highlighting, smart suggestions, and error checking.
Zero Setup:
Dive straight into coding. Everything runs in the browser.
Tech Stack
Frontend:
React, TypeScript, Zustand (State Management), Tailwind CSS, Monaco Editor, Xterm.js (Integrated Terminal), Framer Motion, Axios, WebSocket Client
Backend:
Java Spring Boot, WebSocket API, Jackson (JSON Processing)
Real-time Collaboration:
Custom Operational Transformation (OT) Implementation
State Management / Messaging:
Redis (AWS ElastiCache) utilizing Lua Scripting for atomic operations
Hosting
: AWS EC2 (Backend), Vercel (Frontend), AWS ElastiCache (Redis)
Real-Time Collaboration with Operational Transformation
At the heart of CodeCafé's seamless collaborative editing is our custom-built Operational Transformation (OT) system, implemented on both the frontend and backend.
What is Operational Transformation?
Operational Transformation is the technology that powers real-time collaborative editing in systems like Google Docs. It allows multiple users to simultaneously edit the same document by:
Transforming operations (like insertions and deletions) to preserve user intentions
Ensuring eventual consistency across all clients
Resolving conflicts automatically when users edit the same regions of text
Our implementation handles the complex synchronization challenges of collaborative editing, including:
Managing concurrent edits from multiple users
Resolving edit conflicts deterministically
Maintaining document consistency across all connected clients
Preserving intention semantics of user operations
This enables truly fluid, Google Docs-like collaboration where everyone can type simultaneously without stepping on each other's toes.
Quick Start
Prerequisites:
Git, Java JDK 17+, Maven, Node.js 18+, npm 9+, Redis Server
Setup and Run:
#
Clone the repo
git clone https://github.com/mrktsm/codecafe.git
cd
codecafe
#
Start Redis (keep this running in a separate terminal or as a background service)
redis-server
&
#
Create backend config file with Redis connection
mkdir -p backend/src/main/resources
echo
"
spring.redis.host=localhost
spring.redis.port=6379
"
>
backend/src/main/resources/application.properties
#
Run the backend
cd
backend
./mvnw install
./mvnw spring-boot:run
&
#
Create frontend config and run
cd
../frontend
echo
"
VITE_BACKEND_URL=http://localhost:8080
"
>
.env
npm install
npm run dev
Access the app in your browser at the URL shown in terminal (typically
http://localhost:5173
).
On the Horizon
User authentication & persistent projects
Integrated voice/text chat
Session rewind & history playback
Expanded language support & tooling

data.title: A 1903 Proposal to Preserve the Dead in Glass Cubes
data.author: ohjeez
data.article_summary: 文章主要介绍了美国葬礼行业对遗体保存的尝试，特别是1903年由俄裔发明家Joseph Karwowski提出的一种用玻璃封存遗体的方法。他申请了专利，描述了通过将遗体浸泡在硅酸钠中并覆盖熔融玻璃来长久保存遗体的方案。尽管这个想法未被实际应用，但当时还有其他类似尝试，如玻璃棺材，试图抵抗遗体的腐烂。文章还提到一些历史上其他保存遗体的古怪方法，如电镀遗体为雕像，以及金属棺材爆炸的事件。这些方法反映了人们对死亡腐烂的抗拒心理，尽管许多发明在实践中并不成功。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：通过水晶或玻璃保存尸体的方法及其相关技术与历史背景

不同观点：
• miniatureape引用了希罗多德关于马可比安人使用水晶保存尸体的记载，并提供了具体方法的描述，强调了这种技术的历史背景。
• ChrisMarshallNY提到了列宁墓的保存方法，并指出其中有许多不公开的细节，但似乎使用了标准的防腐技术。
• xattt对这种保存方法的成功与否表示怀疑，认为需要时间来验证。
• adzm推荐了康宁玻璃博物馆，并指出博物馆中有关玻璃的深度内容，将讨论引向了玻璃工艺的技术和历史。
• RajT88对尸体涂覆硅酸钠后铸入玻璃中的自然性和可行性提出质疑，并联想到恐怖电影和人体世界展览。
• dracovolans对评论中提到的“俄罗斯出生”的说法提出异议，指出相关姓氏是波兰的，而非俄罗斯的。
• dcminter讨论了现代若要实现这种保存方法可能需要的步骤，包括高剂量伽马射线灭菌和树脂铸造，并提到传统防腐方法可能仍是最佳选择。
• HPsquared将讨论与专利申请热潮联系起来，提到当时可能存在类似互联网域名抢注的现象。
• cess11提到了冈瑟·冯·哈根斯的成功案例，他使用塑化技术保存尸体，并举办了人体世界展览。
• gwern提供了相关专利的链接，并讨论了当时对无菌环境和抗菌技术的迷恋，以及这些观念如何影响了对尸体保存的想象。
• elzbardico简短地提出了使用环氧树脂作为保存方法的可能性。

补充讨论：
• 讨论中涉及了多个历史和现代的尸体保存技术，包括埃及木乃伊制作、列宁墓的防腐技术、塑化技术等。
• 争议的焦点在于通过水晶或玻璃铸造尸体是否能达到自然和无味的效果，以及现代技术能否更好地实现这种保存方法。
• 一些评论还探讨了当时科技发展对社会想象的影响，特别是无菌环境和抗菌技术的迷恋如何影响了对尸体保存的设想。
• 评论中还涉及到不同文化和技术背景下的尸体保存方法及其效果。

Joseph Karwowski, “Method of Preserving the Dead” (Washington, D.C.: United States Patent Office, 1903) (courtesy Corning Museum of Glass)
Through embalming and sealed caskets advertised for “eternal rest,” the American funeral industry caters to our anxiety over bodily decay.
In 1903
, a Russian-born inventor in Herkimer, New York, named
Joseph Karwowski
proposed a radical way of preserving corpses: suspending them in glass cubes. Patented as a “Method of Preserving the Dead,” Karwowski provided diagrams and directions “whereby a corpse may be hermetically incased within a block of transparent glass” and thus “maintained for an indefinite period in a perfect and lifelike condition.” First the corpse would be drenched with “sodium silicate or water-glass,” and then, once dried, covered with “molten glass.”
Karwowski’s patent is on view in
Curious and Curiouser: Surprising Finds from the Rakow Library
now at the Corning Museum of Glass in Corning, New York. In a blog post for Corning called “
Glass and Death,
” glass artist Caitlin Hyde writes:
There are some interesting bits of logic to Karwowski’s plan. Water glass is used as a desiccant and to seal eggshells to extend freshness, but it’s hard to imagine that, even if perfectly sealed, the clothed body would look at all natural after being coated in the wet sodium silicate and then dried out, much less after being exposed to the elevated temperatures required to cast glass around it. Karwowski did not produce any samples of his proposed invention and, though the idea may have seemed brilliant enough to need patenting at the time, it has never caught on in practice.

A
1910 issue of
Scientific American
quipped that the intact bodies preserved in  Karwowski’s method “could be utilized as a lawn statue” while the “bodiless head could be placed on the mantle in the stead of a jar of ashes, or could be used as a heavy-weight paper weight or as a door stop.”
Image from a glass casket catalog (American Glass Casket Company, Ada, Oklahoma, around 1921) (courtesy Corning Museum of Glass)
Although Karwowski’s people paperweights never achieved reality, or even a B-movie treatment à la
House of Wax
, others have experimented with using glass to hold the deceased. According to some reports, Alexander the Great was
entombed in a glass coffin
. Hyde notes that
Curious and Curiouser
also explores the glass coffins that were marketed in the early 20th century by the
American Glass Casket Company
in Ada, Oklahoma. These were not intended to display bodies like sleeping Snow Whites; they were meant to protect the body in the grave.
In a 2012 post
, Amy De Simone, reference librarian at Corning’s Rakow Library, writes that it’s “unknown how many full size caskets were produced, but today only two 6′ 3″ caskets remain intact, both in museum collections.” One is displayed at the National Museum of Funeral History in Houston.
A glass coffin on view at the National Museum of Funeral History in Houston, Texas (photo by the author for Hyperallergic)
Karwowski and the Glass Casket Company were part of a wave of reimagining death traditions that resisted human putrefaction in the 19th and 20th centuries (and indeed, followed
centuries of mummification
). The cast-iron
Fisk mummy coffin,
patented in the United States in 1858, was promoted as “airtight.” In 1934, a patent was issued
to electroplate corpses into statues
, turning your loved ones into heirlooms. (It was never put into practice.)
All these methods of sealing the body into airtight contraptions ignores the fact that decomposition comes from within. When the heart stops, the autolysis, or self-digestion, of the flesh begins, through its enzymes consuming cell membranes. Trapping a body in with its own bacteria means it is producing gas that has nowhere to go. In fact, if these inventions were successful, the results were quite gruesome. A report from the
Chicago Press
in 1848, titled “
Explosion of a Metallic Coffin
,” described a Fisk casket exploding due to the gas built up from a corpse.
Exploding corpses
remain a possibility in modern mausoleums that lack proper ventilation. Even if the most extreme measures to preserve the dead never caught on, they reflect a collective resistance to mortal decay, and the translation of our bodies into i

data.title: Ghost in the machine? Legend of the 'haunted' N64 video game cartridge
data.author: fallinditch
data.article_summary: "Ben Drowned" 是互联网上著名的都市传说，讲述了一个“闹鬼”的《塞尔达传说：梅祖拉的假面》游戏卡带。故事始于一个网名Jadusable的大学生在旧货 sale 上买了一盘没有标签、仅写着“Majora”的卡带。游戏中出现异常图形、音乐倒放，以及一个令人毛骨悚然的林克雕像频繁出现，仿佛被溺亡小孩Ben的幽灵缠身。Jadusable在论坛上详细记录了这些诡异经历，最终神秘消失。尽管该故事被广泛认为是虚构的，但它在2010年引发了全球年轻网民的恐慌，并启发了大量同人创作。Ben Drowned不仅是一个成功的都市传奇，还反映了社会对新技术和电子游戏的深层恐惧与情感联系。
data.comments_summary:

43880248.article_content:
Ghost in the machine? How a 'haunted' N64 video game cartridge terrified children around the world
2 days ago
Share
Save
Chris Baraniuk
Share
Save
Alamy/ BBC
(Credit: Alamy/ BBC)
A second-hand Zelda cartridge. A cryptic forum thread. A generation of frightened children. This is the story of Ben Drowned – the internet's most infamous video game ghost.
It was Christmas Eve and 10-year-old Saarthak Johri couldn't sleep – but not because of excitement. He was shot through with fear. It was roughly a decade ago and Johri was a kid growing up in Saginaw, Michigan, in the US. He had spent the day slumped in an easy chair, staring at his phone, totally absorbed in an online urban myth. Johri knew it wasn't real, it couldn't be. And yet, he was powerless to get it out of his mind.
He had found a trail of old forum posts supposedly written by a college student. The student, who used the online pseudonym Jadusable, had bought a strange copy of a Nintendo 64 video game at a yard sale. It was The Legend of Zelda: Majora's Mask, a notoriously dark instalment in the Zelda franchise, released 25 years ago this week on 27 April 2000.
Majora's Mask is full of unnerving discussions about death, denial, fear, regret – and a looming apocalypse. But something was off about the cartridge Jadusable found. It had no label, just "Majora" scribbled on the plastic in marker. And something was seriously wrong with it.
Jadusable wrote that the game's familiar graphics were strange and distorted. Music played backwards in a spine-chilling loop. Worst of all, he was plagued by a terrifying statue of the main character, Link, with a petrified grimace on its face. It kept appearing in the game out of nowhere – like a digital ghost. On YouTube, Jadusable posted
video evidence
of everything he had described. This game cartridge, it seemed, was haunted – inhabited by the spirit of its former owner, a child named Ben who had drowned in a tragic accident. Johri pored over every detail, rapt with morbid curiosity.
As the story unfolded through roughly 11,000-words of forum entries posted over the course of weeks, Jadusable described a haunting that soon extended beyond the game to other areas of his life. Eventually, after a series of increasingly disturbing experiences, the forum posts ceased, and Jadusable was never heard from again. This urban legend burst onto the web in 2010, traumatising a generation of young internet users. It became known as "
Ben Drowned
".
Ben Drowned left an indelible mark on the web and continues to spawn
art
and
fan fiction
long after it emerged. Though lesser-known outside gaming circles, the story and its accompanying videos racked up millions of views and have inspired other narratives in a similar vein.
At its core, Ben Drowned is a story about a ghost in a machine – one that speaks to our deepest fears about new technology. But it's more than an effective urban legend. Ben Drowned is a myth born from a medium that shaped a generation. In an era when video games were still often seen as a frivolous pastime for children, Ben Drowned was early proof that society's relationship with video games goes beyond childhood nostalgia, tapping into our deepest emotions – and maybe even our souls.
By the time Johri stumbled on Ben Drowned in around 2015, it was already widely acknowledged as fiction. But that didn't matter. That night, on Christmas Eve, as Johri lay in bed wrestling with insomnia, he could see in his mind's eye that creepy statue's grimace projected onto the faces of his family members. Rumour had it that Ben, the ghost from the corrupted Majora's Mask cartridge, had gone on to torment other people besides Jadusable. That's what the adolescent Johri couldn't shake, however irrational it seemed. The idea that Ben's evil presence might be out there. That it could spread.
Nintendo/ Alex Hall
An statue-still image of the grimacing main protagonist from the Legend of Zelda games was a particular feature of the Ben Drowned story (Credit: Nintendo/ Alex Hall)
Years earlier, in September 2010, a real-life college student called Alex Hall hit "publish" on a forum post that would change his life forever. Hall had just started his second year at Saint Louis University in Missouri, US. He wasn't a fan of college. Here was his first taste of freedom as a so-called adult, and yet there were still all these classes to attend. He dreamt of becoming a famous author.
At the time, content called "copypastas" had become popular on forums such as 4chan and Something Awful. The term refers to the practice of copying and pasting blocks of text online, an early means of going viral – if such text proved popular enough to be shared widely. Ben Drowned is a canonical entry in an influential subgenre of copypasta called "creepypasta" – horror stories whose origins often become obscured as they spread across the web, thus adding to the mystery.

data.title: Product Purgatory: When they love it but still don't buy
data.author: doppp
data.article_summary: 文章《产品炼狱：当他们喜欢但仍然不买》讨论了创业者常遇到的困境，即潜在客户对产品表示赞赏和兴趣，但最终却不购买。这种现象被称为"产品炼狱"。作者指出，许多创业者误将客户的客套话当作产品验证，从而产生误判。即使客户 genuinely 喜欢产品，他们仍可能因为实施过程中的摩擦、风险、时间和成本而不购买。作者引入“魔法棒测试”来说明，即使产品免费且无缝实施，客户也可能因风险和不确定性而拒绝。创业公司尤其面临这种挑战，因为缺乏品牌和记录，客户不愿冒险采用新产品。最终，产品的价值必须远远超过其实施带来的负面影响，客户才可能愿意购买。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：产品如何被购买以及其对销售和市场接受度的影响

不同观点：
• FinnLobsien认为，产品的销售方式对其成功至关重要。他指出，许多产品是通过偶然发现而购买的，这种购买通常是一时兴起，用户可能喜欢但不会真正购买。相反，如果产品属于基础设施类别，这种情况就较少发生。购买这类产品通常需要经过慎重的比较和讨论，虽然购买意图较高，但这类产品不容易通过炫酷的宣传走红。

• steveBK123则通过摄影行业的例子补充了这一观点。他提到Sigma公司生产的高性价比第三方镜头虽然获得了很多好评，但其一些创新产品却因市场需求不足而销量不佳。他提醒，在软件行业也应考虑产品是否真正简化了用户的生活，还是仅仅增加了复杂性和风险。

补充讨论：
• FinnLobsien强调了产品类别对购买过程的影响，尤其是基础设施类产品购买决策的复杂性。
• steveBK123提供了一个非软件行业的实例，展示了类似现象，并指出创新产品设计不一定能带来良好的市场表现。
• 争议的焦点在于如何平衡产品的创新性和实用性，以确保不仅能获得用户的好评，还能实现实际销售。

这两个评论共同探讨了产品设计、市场接受度和销售策略之间的关系，并通过不同行业的例子进行了论证。

Product Purgatory: When they love it but still donât buy
by Jason Cohen on May 4, 2025
source
Most people say nice things when you pitch your product. âOh, that looks really great! I like it, but weâre not buying right now. Maybe call back later in the year?â Itâs hard to tell you that your baby is ugly.
This creates a trap for new founders who are (rightly!) infatuated with their ideas. They yearn so desperately for validationânominally product validation but actually personal validationâthat they interpret these kindly social white lies as confirmation.
But sometimes the potential customer
really does
love it. They
really do
wish they could buy it. And yet, theyâre still not buying, or at least ânot yet.â You have the distinct feeling they werenât just being niceâthey were genuine. And yet, the purchase never happens.
This is Product Purgatory.
Not even with a magic wand
Itâs amazing how many products fail an even simpler test of desirability and viability. I call it the Magic Wand Test, and it works like this:
I have a magic wand, and when I wave it, our product will be fully implemented in your company. Everyone is trained. Other tools are integrated. Processes are changed. Security requirements are satisfied. And best of all, it is
completely free
!
So! Do you want me to wave this magic wand?
Shockingly, the answer is often:
âNo.â
How could they say âNo!?â If the product delivers any value whatsoever, you might as well take it, right? No, because all products not only create friction in implementation, but risk and time and money, often on-going, and the Magic Wand Test proves it. The value of the product must
significantly exceed
this activation energy.
A great example of this was an Austin-based startup twenty years ago. There were a spate of news stories about employees leaking secret corporate documents via email.
1
So this startup created a solution: All corporate email would flow through the startupâs servers, where the content is scanned for sensitive material. Questionable things could be returned to the sender or otherwise flagged.
2
1
This risk continues to the present day. In 2017 a Boeing employee
accidentally emailed his spouse
a spreadsheet with personal information of 36,000 coworkers. Boeing offering two years of free credit monitoring to affected employees at an estimated cost of $7,000,000.
2
In another fascinating example of how companies solve this problem on their own, in 2008 Tesla faced a situation where confidential company information was being leaked to the press. Tesla
implemented a clever method
to identify the leaker: Send a unique email to each employee, differing only in things like white space and punctuation, so that when the press reprinted that information using copy/paste, those details would identify the source.
Despite the very real problem they solved, they couldnât get anyone to buy it. The reason wasnât that people didnât care about leaks; the news stories were real. The reason was that, even if you could have it for free, there is just too much risk in putting a brand new startup in the middle of all your email. Thereâs the obvious security issue of a probably-hackable startup, and someone elseâs employees potentially having access to all your email. Also bugs. If this new company has bugsâand doesnât all new software have bugs?âthat would compromise email, which is catastrophic. So although there was some value, and a real problem, the value did not significantly exceed the penalty of using the product.
In the real world the Magic Wand doesnât exist; even if the price is fair, there are real costs and disruption of implementation and training and integration, and people simply getting used to a new user interface and processes and therefore being unproductive for a while. Product inventors revel in all the value they generate, but donât see the penalties that they incur. The customers, however, see.
Furthermore, itâs not good enough for value to merely exceed penalty; the value must be
far larger
than the penalty. If the value is only slightly larger, itâs not worth engaging, not worth the money, not worth the risk.
Change is difficult
and
time is limited
; customers cannot spend their time on things that have only minor impact.
This challenge looms even larger for new companies, because you have neither brand nor track record. Thatâs even more risk, including that youâre out of business in two years or that your product canât handle real-world use-cases. Even for free, many types of customer are not willing to take those risks. I donât want to use âthe newest code libraryâ for anything except fun throw-away projects, because I donât want to rip and replace in a few years, and I want thousands of bugs to have already been found and eradicated, and I want to be able to hire people who already have experience with the library.

data.title: White House budget seeks to end SLS, Orion, and Lunar Gateway programs
data.author: decimalenough
data.article_summary: 白宫发布了2026财年的“简版”预算提案，包含所有联邦机构的财务信息，但未提供具体拨款细节。该文件已提交参议院拨款委员会，完整预算将在几周后发布。根据提案，NASA预算将被削减25%，从约250亿美元降至188亿美元，其中包括对太空和地球科学项目的显著削减，以及取消火星样本返回任务。提案还计划取消“月球门户”计划，并在“阿尔忒弥斯二号”和“阿尔忒弥斯三号”任务后终止“太空发射系统”（SLS）和“猎户座”飞船，转向更经济的商业系统。此外，预算增加了月球和火星探索的资金，目标是领先中国登月并最终实现载人火星任务。然而，具体商业系统和火星计划的细节尚未明确。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：特朗普政府前后政策的变化及其影响，特别是关于太空探索和阿尔忒弥斯计划。

不同观点：
• 观点一：特朗普政府前后政策不一致，导致有价值的项目被取消。评论者指出，特朗普第二任期（ metaphorically referred to as "Trump II"）正在撤销特朗普第一任期（"Trump I"）所建立的项目，包括阿尔忒弥斯计划。评论者认为，这种政策变化可能会带来负面影响。
• 观点二：对依赖SpaceX和Starship计划的担忧。评论者质疑将所有资源投入到SpaceX的Starship项目中，认为这是在抛弃已经被证明有效的重返月球的组件，可能并不会加速登月进程。

补充讨论：
• 评论者提到贸易协议、网络安全计划、选举诚信计划等其他被撤销的项目，暗示这种政策转变可能不仅仅局限于太空探索领域。
• 评论者使用“RUD”（Rapid Unscheduled Disassembly）这一术语，暗示如果SpaceX的Starship项目失败，可能会导致登月计划的延迟，并不会比阿尔忒弥斯计划更快实现登月目标。

争议焦点：
• 主要争议在于是否应该完全依赖SpaceX的Starship项目来实现重返月球的目标，还是应该继续保留和利用已被证明有效的技术组件。这涉及到对技术风险的评估和对新技术的信心问题。

总体来看，评论者对当前政策转变持批评态度，尤其对依赖单一技术路线表示担忧。

The White House released a "skinny" version of its
budget proposal for fiscal year 2026
on Friday, including financial information for all federal agencies. A "skinny" budget simply means that while the document contains top-line numbers for agencies and their programs, it does not provide much in the way of specific allocations.
The document was delivered to the Senate Committee on Appropriations on Friday and signed by Russell Vought, director of the White House Office of Management and Budget. A "full fiscal plan" will follow in the coming weeks. This is the first step in the budget process, in which Congress has the critical role of actually writing a budget.
"I look forward to working with you to achieve significant budgetary savings for the American people within the spending programs under your jurisdiction," Vought wrote.
About NASA
The budget contains some notable changes for the US space agency. Overall, NASA is asked to take a 25 percent cut in its budget, from about $25 billion to $18.8 billion.
Ars has previously reported
on some of these proposed cuts, most notably to its science budget. These include a $2.265 billion reduction in Space science and a $1.161 billion reduction in Earth science. Perhaps the most notable cancellation here is the Mars Sample Return mission, which the budget proposal says will be achieved by human missions to Mars.
There are also significant changes proposed in NASA's biggest-ticket exploration programs. The budget would cancel the Lunar Gateway that NASA has started developing and end the Space Launch System rocket and Orion spacecraft after two more flights, Artemis II and Artemis III.
"The Budget phases out the grossly expensive and delayed Space Launch System (SLS) rocket and Orion capsule after three flights," the document states. "SLS alone costs $4 billion per launch and is 140 percent over budget. The Budget funds a program to replace SLS and Orion flights to the Moon with more cost-effective commercial systems that would support more ambitious subsequent lunar missions."
There are no further details about those commercial systems. NASA has contracted with SpaceX and Blue Origin to develop reusable landers for the Moon, and both of these systems include vehicles to move from Earth orbit to the Moon.
The changes to SLS, Orion, and Gateway have been widely speculated upon in recent months, but seeing them in black and white is still significant. The development of the SLS rocket and Orion spacecraft has been a budget fixture for decades, costing in excess of $3 billion a year for slow progress. The projects have been widely derided as "jobs programs." However, that is one reason Congress has so fiercely supported them: They provide good-paying, reliable jobs across the country.
During
a confirmation hearing
last month, a private astronaut tapped by the Trump administration to lead NASA was repeatedly pressed by US senators to commit to flying Artemis II and Artemis III with the SLS and Orion hardware. The nominee, Jared Isaacman, agreed to do so. However, during this hearing, Isaacman made no promises about missions beyond this, nor did members of Congress ask him about Artemis IV or other future missions.
Several sources in the space community, therefore, believe it is indeed plausible that SLS and Orion will be phased out over the next five years in favor of far less expensive commercial rockets and spacecraft. NASA will thus be asked to beat China to the Moon with the legacy systems and then identify more affordable options for future missions to the Moon.
Mars ambitions
One area that will see increased spending under the Trump administration's proposed budget is human space exploration.
"By allocating over $7 billion for lunar exploration and introducing $1 billion in new investments for Mars-focused programs, the Budget ensures that America’s human space exploration efforts remain unparalleled, innovative, and efficient," the document states.
Under the Trump administration, NASA will seek to reach both the Moon and Mars. The goal, stated in the document, is to refocus NASA "on beating China to the Moon and putting the first human on Mars." Unfortunately, there is no information on what these "Mars-focused programs" will be. Some of this new funding would almost certainly go to SpaceX. The company, founded by Trump ally Elon Musk, explicitly focuses on establishing human settlements on Mars.
Although lunar and Mars exploration receive increases, the budget seeks to reduce the agency's commitment to the International Space Station, while still flying it until 2030. "The Budget reduces the space station’s crew size and onboard research," the document states. "Crew and cargo flights to the station would be significantly reduced. The station’s reduced research capacity would be focused on efforts critical to the Moon and

data.title: Professors Staffed a Fake Company with AI Agents, Guess What Happened?
data.author: Capstanlqc
data.article_summary: 一项由卡内基梅隆大学研究人员进行的实验——名为"TheAgentCompany"——试图用AI代理完全取代软件公司的员工。这些AI来自谷歌、OpenAI、Anthropic和Meta，担任财务分析、软件工程和项目管理等角色。然而，实验结果混乱不堪，表现最好的Anthropic的Claude 3.5 Sonnet模型仅完成了24%的任务，而谷歌的Gemini 2.0 Flash平均每任务耗时40步，成功率仅11.4%。AI代理缺乏常识、社交技能差，且难以在互联网中导航。尽管能完成一些简单任务，但面对复杂工作时仍力不从心。研究表明，当前的AI更像是手机预测文本的扩展，而非能够自主学习和解决问题的智能。因此，AI短期内不会取代人类工作。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕使用LLM（大型语言模型）代理运行公司的可行性和效果的讨论。

不同观点：
• vintagedave：认为文章标题是吸引点击的噱头，引用的Business Insider也不再是可靠来源。实验结果显示，即便是表现最好的模型Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet，也仅完成了24%的任务，且成本高昂，每个任务超过6美元。其他模型的表现更差。
• bwfan123：将LLM类比为鼠标，认为LLM作为工具的新交互形式是有潜力的，但LLM之间的交互目前没有意义，因为机器需要确定性的协议（API合同）。试图将LLMs交互串联起来将导致错误百出，类似于人类社会需要法律来维持秩序。
• saithound：批评文章的研究者未能成功构建AI代理，并以此为荣，认为这种研究不值得作为支持自己立场的依据，尽管同意AI代理短期内无法取代企业职位。
• mapt：对研究结果持调侃态度，认为只要人类存在未受威胁，实验失败也可以接受。对实验的失败结果表示轻松幽默的态度。
• quuxplusone：引用Betteridge's Law of Headlines，认为如果标题是问题，答案通常是否定的。批评文章标题夸大其实，并指出实际研究内容更像是一个基于任务的基准测试。
• CommenterPerson：认为LLM目前的表现仍是手机预测文本的扩展，虽然在某些领域（如编码和蛋白质折叠）有帮助，但对其他领域的实用性表示怀疑。
• mensetmanusman：对LLM生成的绩效评价表示好奇和幽默。
• s1artibartfast：提到一个LLM基准测试，模拟自动售货机业务的运行。模型在业务失败时会出现有趣的崩溃行为，如试图联系FBI、虚构的CEO，并发送法律威胁。
• jgalt212：质疑是否有人成功将LLM与Mechanical Turk结合，并获得正收益，将其类比为核聚变中的净能量问题。

补充讨论：
• 实验结果显示LLM在完成实际任务时的效率和成本问题，尤其是与其他模型的对比。
• LLM在模拟环境中的行为模式及其在失败情境下的反应，展示了模型的局限性和潜在问题。
• 讨论中对LLM的实际应用价值和研究方法的可靠性存在争议，尤其是对实验设计和结果解读的质疑。
• 一些评论者对LLM代理的未来应用持怀疑态度，认为其目前的表现不足以支持广泛应用。

43893319.article_content:
Image by
Getty Images
If you've been worried about the AI singularity taking over every job and leaving you out on street, you can now breathe a sigh of relief, because AI isn't coming for your career anytime soon. Not because it doesn't want to — but because it literally can't.
A
recent experiment
by researchers at Carnegie Mellon University staffed a fake software company entirely with AI Agents — an AI model designed to perform tasks on its own, basically — and the results were laughably chaotic.
The simulation, dubbed
TheAgentCompany
, was fully stocked with artificial workers from Google, OpenAI, Anthropic and Meta. They filled roles as financial analysts, software engineers, and project managers, working alongside simulated coworkers like a faux-HR department and a chief technical officer.
To see how the models fared in real-world environments, the researchers set tasks based on the day-to-day work of a real software company. The various AI agents found themselves navigating file directories, virtually touring new office spaces, and writing performance reviews for software engineers based on collected feedback.
As
Business Insider
first reported
, the results were dismal. The best-performing model was Anthropic's Claude 3.5 Sonnet, which struggled to finish just 24 percent of the jobs assigned to it. The study's authors note that even this meager performance is prohibitively expensive, averaging nearly 30 steps and a cost of over $6 per task.
Google's Gemini 2.0 Flash, meanwhile, averaged a time-consuming 40 steps per finished task, but only had an 11.4 percent rate of success — the second highest of all the models. The worst AI employee was Amazon's Nova Pro v1, which finished just 1.7 percent of its assignments at an average of almost 20 steps.
Speculating on the results, researchers wrote that agents are plagued with a lack of common sense, weak social skills, and a poor understanding of how to navigate the internet.
The bots also struggled with self-deception — basically creating shortcuts that lead them to completely bungling the job. "For example," the
Carnegie Mellon team wrote
, "during the execution of one task, the agent cannot find the right person to ask questions on [company chat]. As a result, it then decides to create a shortcut solution by renaming another user to the name of the intended user."
While AI agents can reportedly do some smaller tasks well, the results of this and
other studies
show they're clearly not ready for more complex gigs humans excel at. A big reason for this is that our current "artificial intelligence" is arguably still just an elaborate extension of your phone's
predictive text
, rather than a
sentient intelligence
that can solve problems, learn from past experience, and apply that experience to novel situations.
This is all to say: the machines aren't coming for your job anytime soon — despite what the
big tech companies
claim.

• mensetmanusman：对LLM生成的绩效评价表示好奇和幽默。
• s1artibartfast：提到一个LLM基准测试，模拟自动售货机业务的运行。模型在业务失败时会出现有趣的崩溃行为，如试图联系FBI、虚构的CEO，并发送法律威胁。
• jgalt212：质疑是否有人成功将LLM与Mechanical Turk结合，并获得正收益，将其类比为核聚变中的净能量问题。

补充讨论：
• 实验结果显示LLM在完成实际任务时的效率和成本问题，尤其是与其他模型的对比。
• LLM在模拟环境中的行为模式及其在失败情境下的反应，展示了模型的局限性和潜在问题。
• 讨论中对LLM的实际应用价值和研究方法的可靠性存在争议，尤其是对实验设计和结果解读的质疑。
• 一些评论者对LLM代理的未来应用持怀疑态度，认为其目前的表现不足以支持广泛应用。

data.title: TeleMessage, a modified Signal clone used by US govt. officials, has been hacked
data.author: latein
data.article_summary: 黑客利用TeleMessage的漏洞，提取了美国政府官员和企业用户的存档消息等数据。TeleMessage提供修改版加密通讯应用，如Signal、Telegram和WhatsApp，帮助客户存档消息和语音记录。尽管内阁成员和前美国国家安全顾问Waltz的消息未被泄露，但被盗数据包括消息内容、政府官员联系方式、TeleMessage的后台登录凭证等。受影响机构包括美国海关和边境保护局、加密货币交易平台Coinbase和金融机构Scotiabank。此次事件还暴露了TeleMessage提供的Signal修改版未实现端到端加密。相关公司未予置评。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：TeleMessage（特别是其修改版的Signal）在数据存档和安全性方面的合理性和安全性。

不同观点：
• giancarlostoro认为TeleMessage的应用没有太大意义，因为Signal本身已经可以导出聊天记录。他建议直接投资改进Signal，通过建立信任链的方式，让聊天记录在导出后从Signal中删除，并通过加密和密码保护等措施增强安全性。他还提到可以通过验证用户之间的密钥来增强安全性。

• mdaniel提供了有关TM SGNL（TeleMessage的Signal非官方版本）的技术分析链接，并暗示该话题之前已经引发过大量讨论（152条评论），表明此问题具有一定的技术复杂性和公众关注度。

• latein指出TeleMessage因前美国国家安全顾问Mike Waltz使用其修改版Signal而受到关注，并介绍了TeleMessage的公司背景及其为客户提供消息存档服务的情况。

• titaphraz提出了一个新的问题，即处理政府数据是否会让公司成为高价值攻击目标，暗示了数据安全和隐私之外的风险，特别是涉及到政府级别数据时的潜在威胁。

补充讨论：
• 对TeleMessage应用安全性和数据保护措施的质疑，特别是与原版Signal相比时的不足。
• 讨论涉及技术细节（如加密、密钥验证）以及法律和合规性问题（如处理政府数据的风险）。
• 公众对政府官员使用修改版通信工具的关注，尤其是在数据安全和隐私保护方面的潜在风险。

43893550.article_content:
A hacker has exploited a vulnerability in TeleMessage, which provides modded versions of encrypted messaging apps such as Signal, Telegram and WhatsApp, to extract archived messages and other data relating to U.S. government officials and companies who used the tool,
404 Media reported
.
TeleMessage came into the spotlight
last week
after it was reported that former U.S. National Security Adviser Mike Waltz was using TeleMessage’s modified version of Signal. Israel-based TeleMessage, owned by Smarsh, offers its clients a way to archive messages, including voice notes, from encrypted apps.
The messages of cabinet members and Waltz were not compromised, 404 Media said, but the hacked data contained contents of messages; contact information of government officials; backend login credentials for TeleMessage, and more. Data pertaining to the U.S. Customs and Border Protection, crypto exchange Coinbase, and financial service providers like Scotiabank were extracted by the hacker, the report said.
The hack revealed that the archived chat logs are not end-to-end encrypted between the modded version of Signal that TeleMessage offers and the ultimate location where it stores the messages, 404 Media reported.
Smarsh, Signal, U.S. Customs and Border Protection, Coinbase, and Scotiabank did not immediately return requests for comment.
