data.title: The Design of Compact Elastic Binary Trees (Cebtree)
data.author: r4um
data.article_summary: 本文介绍了作者在周末项目中对紧凑弹性二叉树（compact elastic binary trees）的探索和优化过程。最初，作者在2007年开发ebtrees时，发现自组织树可以在不向上遍历的情况下处理插入、删除和访问操作。通过XOR算法优化查找过程后，作者进一步简化了树结构，仅使用两个指针构建完整的树，而不需要存储深度或其它信息。2014年，作者将这一概念应用到名为“water drop alloc”的内存分配器中，利用指针本身作为键来索引节点，实现了高度紧凑的树结构，节省了存储空间。这一项目展示了通过XOR比较和自组织特性实现高效查找和紧凑存储的可能性。
data.comments_summary: 暂无评论

43893225.article_content:
Those who often hear me discuss about my week-end projects have been accustomed to hearing about deuterium fusion (that's for another post), laser engraving, and the compact version of the ebtrees, aka compact elastic binary trees, without knowing all the details. That's what we'll be discussing here.
A long history
Self-organizing trees
It started very early during the development of
ebtrees
, in which the same node appears twice, once as a node and once as a leaf. In 2007, when
I managed to build self-organizing trees to handle duplicates
, and noticed that all that was needed to insert, delete, and visit nodes, was to remember the node from which to restart or where to attach, and that it was never needed to go upwards in the tree for such operations, that made me think that maybe this type of structure would also work to arrange data without uplink and without keeping any relation between the node's depth and the key it conveys. Adding a new duplicate value would only require to measure the depth of the penultimate branch and allow to grow the next one until it becomes as long. If it was already as long, then another one just had to be added above it. For example below, we're adding 4 successive entries to a duplicate sub-tree that already contains 4 identical keys ordered by their insertion sequence. The number in the leaf indicates the arrival order for each of them:
XORing branches
18 months later, when
optimizing the lookup algorithm
by comparing the XOR between the looked up key and the node's key with the node's position, I figured that the XOR between the two branches was always necessarily lower given that these branches have more bits in common, and that maybe we could afford not to store the depth if the XOR between the key and node, and the XOR between the two next branches already allowed us to figure where we're located in the tree. An intuition was that, just like in the ebtrees, we can detect that the searched key is not there when the XOR of the two branches is no longer smaller than between the key and current node, or that we're reaching a leaf if the XOR is higher than the previous one.
In the example below, we successively insert the keys 6, 4, then 5. 6 being the first entry, it's the node-less entry (it only has a leaf). Then 4 is inserted, it has 4 and 5 below it, then 5 is inserted below 4, so it has 4 and 5 as its leaves:
In red is indicated the XOR between the branches. The node-less leaf is a special case that loops to itself, so its descendants are the same. 4 splits between 5 and 5, so the XOR of the branches here is
5^6=3
. 5 splits 4 and 5 so its XOR is
4^5=1
.
When descending along the branch to key 4, a XOR of 3 is first met at node 4, then a XOR of 1 is met at node 5, then when going down to node 4 (which is the same as the one on top), we're seeing a XOR of 3 again. 3 being higher than previous value 1 proves that
we have looped, so 4 here is no longer a node but a leaf
.
Similarly, when looking up a value, XORing the searched value with the node's value indicates if we have a chance to find it below or not. As soon as the XOR between a node's branches is higher than the XOR between the looked up value and the node's value, we're certain it cannot be there anymore.
All of this was fun and interesting, but turning intuitions into new week-end projects is never trivial nor necessarily desired when there are already plenty of other activities, so aside a few ideas from time to time when improving ebtrees, not much progress was done in this area for a while.
First limited implementation
Several years later, in 2014, while thinking about a super-compact memory allocator that I'd call "
water drop alloc
" ("
wdalloc
") to illustrate how releasing a drop of water in the middle of two other ones that touches them instantly becomes a larger one, I was thinking that a more compact variant of ebtrees would be particularly suited for that purpose if they would index the pointer itself as the key instead of a stored key. An example of the principle is seen below where freeing a block of length 4 at address 5 results in a new free block of 11 by fusing it with the two adjacent blocks, thanks to trivial adjacent address lookups:
Thus I implemented the "space efficient trees" by then for that purpose, proving that the concept of descending with only two pointers and nothing else is sufficient to build a complete tree:
That's it, only two pointers and nothing else, i.e. 16 bytes on 64-bit architectures. Compared to ebtrees which take 40 bytes (or even 48 with alignment) on such architectures, it's a nice saving!
Here the leaf keys would just be the nodes' addresses, so there was no additional storage, and two pointers were really the only required storage for each allocatable area, with nothing having to be stored for as long as the node is in use.
That application was well suited to the limited experience I had accumulated by then about these new trees:
no need to look up the pointer

data.title: Cursor hits $9B valuation
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 无法获取文章内容
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：围绕Cursor及其相关AI编码工具的评价和争议

不同观点：
• **支持Cursor并强调其效率**：Syzygies认为Cursor在代码审查和AI辅助编码方面非常高效，尤其是在控制Claude Code方面优于其他平台。他认为Claude Code是赢家，尽管成本较高。他选择了Sublime Text作为编辑器，因其快速和简洁。

• **Cursor与vibe coding的区别**：kennu指出Cursor注重高效审查AI提出的更改，而不是像vibe coding那样只关注代码是否有效。他认为Cursor需要用户主动批准更改，而不是盲目接受。

• **对未来编码方式的预测**：jmacd认为未来的编码将不再依赖于传统的IDE编辑器，而是更自动化和直觉化。他指出当前许多工具的使用具有表演性，用户依赖于AI来解决错误和提出更改。

• **Cursor的安全问题**：ndr警告Cursor用户，由于Cursor使用过时的VSCode Marketplace快照，导致一些扩展存在高严重性安全漏洞。尽管问题已被承认，但仍未解决，用户需谨慎使用。

• **Cursor的估值和市场前景**：0x500x79对Cursor的90亿美元估值表示怀疑，认为尽管AI工具已经改变了工作方式，但其未来价值仍不确定。他提到LLM提供商对模型的理解更深入，可能对Cursor构成竞争。

• **对编辑器的看法**：drbojingle认为Cursor不应局限于一个编辑器，建议放弃编辑器功能，让用户自由选择。Zealotux则认为Cursor比VSCode更优秀。

• **多语言支持的疑问**：twodave提问是否不同编程语言需要不同编码代理，或者一个代理就能在所有语言中表现一致。

• **对Cursor商业模式的质疑**：brianbreslin认为Cursor的融资策略可能意味着其计划进入基础设施领域，如Replit的应用托管层。

• **对Cursor估值的惊讶**：CyberMacGyver提到Cursor曾拒绝OpenAI的200亿美元收购提议，现在的估值似乎大幅下降。bix6则对Cursor的2亿美元年收入和45倍的市盈率表示惊讶，质疑为何不选择上市。

• **对媒体描述的不满**：nyrulez对媒体将Cursor描述为vibe coding应用表示不满，认为媒体和影响者与软件工程实际脱节。

补充讨论：
• Cursor的效率和安全问题成为讨论焦点，部分用户对其编辑器功能和市场前景持不同看法。
• 不同用户对AI编码工具的未来发展方向有不同预测，部分认为将更加自动化和直觉化。
• 对Cursor的估值和商业策略存在较大争议，部分用户对其市场表现和融资策略表示怀疑。

data.title: Fuzzy images are our first look at Amazon's super-secret satellites
data.author: NN88
data.article_summary:
亚马逊的Kuiper宽带网络首批生产卫星本周发射，但发射直播非常简短，类似于秘密间谍卫星发射。亚马逊之后在社交媒体上发布了一段40秒的视频，首次展示了Kuiper卫星在太空与运载火箭分离的画面。自2019年亚马逊宣布Kuiper项目以来，公司一直不愿展示卫星的影像。与此不同，其竞争对手SpaceX和OneWeb在发射前公开了卫星的照片和基本信息。

亚马逊的Kuiper卫星呈梯形，设计与OneWeb类似，而与SpaceX的扁平设计不同。亚马逊的首批27颗卫星由联合发射联盟（ULA）的Atlas V火箭送入轨道，发射直播在中途被亚马逊要求停止。卫星逐一从分配器中分离，整个过程未公开。

Kuiper项目负责人Rajeev Badyal曾是SpaceX副总裁，2018年被解雇后加入亚马逊，这使得两家公司的卫星设计对比更加引人关注。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：亚马逊卫星计划对科研和通信的潜在影响

不同观点：
• **[butlike] 担心新增的卫星网络可能干扰深空研究**  
  - 提出问题：越来越多的卫星相互发送信号，是否会影响研究人员“聆听”深空事件的能力。
  - 论据：新增的卫星通信可能会造成电磁波干扰，进而影响射电天文学的研究。
  - 例子：射电望远镜需要安静的电磁环境来捕捉深空信号，卫星通信可能破坏这种环境。

• **[londons_explore] 关注卫星信号的安全性和信息泄露风险**  
  - 提出问题：卫星视频信号是否会被第三方从未加密的下行链路中截获。
  - 论据：如果卫星信号未加密，可能会存在安全隐患，第三方便可能获取敏感信息。
  - 例子：提到未加密的下行链路视频 feed 可能被截获，表明对信息安全的担忧。

补充讨论：
- **争议焦点**：新增卫星网络在科学研究和通信领域的双重影响。一方面是技术进步带来的通信便利，另一方面是对科学研究和信息安全的潜在负面影响。
- **未解答的问题**：评论中提出的两个问题尚未得到明确回答，尤其是在技术细节和解决方案上缺乏深入讨论。

The first production satellites for Amazon's Kuiper broadband network launched earlier this week, but if you tuned in to the mission's official livestream, the truncated coverage had the feel of a spy satellite launch.
This changed with a video Amazon posted on social media Friday, giving space enthusiasts and prospective Kuiper customers their first look at the real satellites. The 40-second clip shows the Kuiper satellites separating from their launch vehicle in the blackness of space following
liftoff Monday
from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida.
Since Amazon unveiled Project Kuiper in 2019, officials at the retail giant have been shy about showing even the most basic imagery of their satellites. Images released by Amazon previously provided glimpses inside the company's satellite factory near Seattle, along with views of the shipping containers Amazon uses to transport spacecraft from Washington to their launch base in Florida.
But none of the images showed what the satellites actually looked like. Ars asked Amazon officials multiple times over the last two years if the company would release pictures of the satellites in production, undergoing launch preparations, or even an artist's illustration. The answer was always no, or not at this time.
This policy contrasts with that of SpaceX, which operates the Starlink network in competition with Kuiper. Starlink is the largest constellation of satellites in orbit, with more than 7,300 spacecraft currently in space. OneWeb operates the second-largest satellite fleet, with more than 650 active satellites. Both constellations broadcast Internet signals with global reach using satellites in low-Earth orbit. SpaceX and OneWeb revealed basic information and photos about their satellites before they ever launched into space.
Amazon is far behind SpaceX in the market for consumer broadband service from space. Amazon aims to launch 3,232 Kuiper satellites on more than 80 rockets, primarily United Launch Alliance's (ULA) Atlas V and Vulcan, over the next few years.
An Atlas V rocket provided the ride to orbit for Amazon's first 27 operational Kuiper satellites Monday. The rocket's Centaur upper stage released the satellites at an altitude of 280 miles (450 kilometers) less than an hour after liftoff.
Amazon requested ULA end the official live broadcast of the launch around five minutes into the flight, barely a quarter of the way through the Atlas V's 18-minute climb into orbit. After reaching orbit, the Centaur upper stage released the Kuiper satellites three at a time from a cylindrical carrier module fastened to the forward end of the rocket.

All of these milestones occurred out of public view, a policy of secrecy similar to the launch of a clandestine military spy satellite. Of course, commercial companies like ULA have no obligation to broadcast their launches at all, and there's no requirement for Amazon to show pictures of its satellites.
The video Amazon released Friday of the Kuiper deployments is fuzzy, and the finer details of the satellites are unseen. However, it's clear enough to make out their basic design.
The Kuiper satellites are trapezoidal in shape. With their solar arrays folded up for launch, they look much like OneWeb's satellites, and a lot different from Starlinks, which have a flatter design to stack one on top of another inside SpaceX's Falcon 9 rocket. SpaceX has used this architecture since the first Starlink launch in 2019, and it was novel at the time. Once in orbit, SpaceX releases tensioners to passively cast free the Starlink satellites all at once, allowing the stack of more than 20 spacecraft to disperse as they begin their missions.
This frame from a SpaceX video shows a stack of Starlink Internet satellites attached to the upper stage of a Falcon 9 rocket, moments after jettison of the launcher's payload fairing.
Credit:
SpaceX
Amazon's satellites were individually mounted to a dispenser for their ride to orbit Monday. Their deployments were staggered over about 15 minutes, with each satellite relying on its own timed separation mechanism.
What might have been

he was fired by Elon Musk in 2018

DNSanity 🎯
Quickly validate DNS servers at scale
Created by
nil0x42
and
contributors
📖 Overview
DNSanity
is a fast DNS resolvers validator, offering deep
customization
and reliable
concurrency
.
If you want to validate massive lists with speed and precision, we have you covered !
Blazing-Fast
: Test thousand servers in parallel, with
global & per-server rate-limiting
.
Flexible
: Easily write your own template for custom validation.
Reliable
: Automatic template re-validation before every usage.
🔃 Workflow
Template Validation (step 1/2)
Make sure template is still valid, matching it against trusted servers.
Servers Sanitization (step 2/2)
For each server, every template test is checked.
If mismatches exceed threshold, server is dropped. Undropped
servers are considered valid.
💡 Quick start
go install github.com/nil0x42/dnsanity@latest
#
go 1.22+ recommended
dnsanity --help
#
show help
dnsanity -list
"
untrustedDNS.txt
"
-o
"
out.txt
"
#
basic usage
📇 Custom template
#
<FQDN>             <EXPECTED-RESULT>                 <COMMENT>
cr.yp.to             A=131.193.32.108 A=131.193.32.109
#
two specific A records
wiki.debian.org      A=
*
CNAME=wilder.debian.org.
#
specific CNAME with any A record
dn05jq2u.fr          NXDOMAIN
#
invalid TLD: NXDOMAIN
dnssec-failed.org    SERVFAIL
#
valid TLD & no records: SERVFAIL
lists.isc.org        A=149.20.
*
#
A record matching pattern
app-c0a801fb.nip.io  A=192.168.1.251
#
specific single A record
retro.localtest.me   A=127.0.0.1
#
specific single A record
A template test
(line)
defines what a domain must return when resolved by a DNS server.
Create your template, and use it with
dnsanity -template /path/to/template.txt
🔍 Options
🏭 Under the Hood
DNSanity
aims for maximum speed without sacrificing reliability
or risking blacklisting. Here’s the core approach:
Trusted Validation
Before checking your untrusted servers, DNSanity verifies the
template
itself against trusted resolvers (e.g.,
8.8.8.8
,
1.1.1.1
).
This ensures your template is valid and consistent.
Test-by-Test Concurrency
For each untrusted server, DNSanity runs tests sequentially in
an efficient pipeline. Once a server accumulates more mismatches than
-max-mismatches
(default 0)
, it’s dropped immediately,
saving time & bandwidth.
Per-Server Rate Limit
Use
-ratelimit
so you don’t overload any single DNS server.
This is especially helpful for fragile networks or for preventing
blacklisting on public resolvers.
Timeout & Retries
If a query doesn’t reply within
-timeout
seconds, it fails.
If
-max-attempts
is greater than 1, DNSanity can retry,
up to the specified limit.
ℹ️ Additional Tips
Craft a Thorough Template
A varied template (involving A, CNAME, NXDOMAIN, and wildcard matches)
quickly exposes shady or broken resolvers.
Geo-Located Domains
Beware that some domains (e.g., google.com) may return different IP addresses
based on location. This might cause expected results to mismatch.
Fine-tune template validation step
-trusted-*
flags allow fine-tuning specific limits for this step, which
uses trusted server list (use
--help
for details)
⭐ Acknowledgments
dnsvalidator
– for the original concept of verifying DNS resolvers.
dnsx
– inspiration for a fast, multi-purpose DNS toolkit.
miekg/dns
– the Go library powering DNSanity queries under the hood.
Happy Recon & Hacking!

data.title: Bootstrapping Lisp in a Boot Sector
data.author: gone35
data.article_summary:
**sectorlisp** 是一个仅 512 字节的 LISP 实现，能够在裸机上启动 John McCarthy 的元循环求值器。该项目旨在通过以下方式简化和实现 LISP：

1. 提供一个纯 LISP 表达式实现，仅使用语言的核心功能，修复了 McCarthy 原论文中的错误并去除语法糖（见 `lisp.lisp`）。
2. 提供一个可读的、可移植的 C 参考实现，展示如何在符合 POSIX 的平台上原生启动元循环求值器，并附带类似 readline 的接口（见 `lisp.c`）。
3. 提供一个可在个人电脑 BIOS 上启动的 512 字节 i8086 LISP 实现（见 `sectorlisp.S`），这是迄今为止最小的完整 LISP 实现。

用户可通过 `make` 命令编译 C 实现，并使用 `sectorlisp.bin` 在模拟器（如 Blinkenlights 或 QEMU）中启动。项目还提供了演示视频展示如何启动和运行。

sectorlisp
sectorlisp is a 512-byte implementation of LISP that's able to bootstrap
John McCarthy's meta-circular evaluator on bare metal.
Overview
LISP has been described as the
Maxwell's equations of
software
.
Yet there's been very little focus to date on reducing these equations
to their simplest possible form. Even the
original LISP
paper
from the 1960's defines LISP with nonessential elements, e.g.
LABEL
.
This project aims to solve that by doing three things:
We provide a LISP implementation that's written in LISP, as a single
pure expression, using only the essential functions of the language.
See
lisp.lisp
. It's the same meta-circular evaluator in
John McCarthy's paper from the 1960's, except with its bugs fixed,
dependencies included, and syntactic sugar removed.
We provide a readable portable C reference implementation to show how
the meta-circular evaluator can be natively bootstrapped on POSIX
conforming platforms, with a pleasant readline-like interface. See
lisp.c
.
We provide a 512-byte i8086 implementation of LISP that boots from
BIOS on personal computers. See
sectorlisp.S
. To the
best of our knowledge, this is the tiniest true LISP implementation
to date.
Getting Started
See
lisp.lisp
for code examples that you can copy and paste
into your LISP REPL.
You can run the C implementation as follows:
$ make
$ ./lisp
After running
make
you should see a
sectorlisp.bin
file, which is a
master boot record you can put on a flopy disk and boot from BIOS. If
you would prefer to run it in an emulator, we recommend using
Das Blinkenlights
.
curl --compressed https://justine.lol/blinkenlights/blinkenlights-latest.com
>
blinkenlights.com
chmod +x blinkenlights.com
./blinkenlights.com -rt sectorlisp.bin
Alternatively you may use QEMU as follows:
qemu-system-i386 -nographic -fda sectorlisp.bin
Further information may be found on
our wiki
.
Demo
The video above demonstrates how to boot sectorlisp in the blinkenlights
emulator, to bootstrap the meta-circular evaluator, which evaluates a
program for finding the first element in a tree.
You can
watch the full demo on YouTube
.

data.title: SpaceX pushed "sniper" theory with the feds
data.author: jnord
data.article_summary: 2016年9月1日，SpaceX在佛罗里达进行Falcon 9火箭静态点火测试时，火箭在发动机点火前意外爆炸，导致火箭及所载Amos-6卫星损毁。这起事故是SpaceX的第二次火箭失败，正值公司与NASA合作的关键时期，引发了广泛关注。由于没有立即找到明确原因，SpaceX内部甚至怀疑是否是外部袭击（“狙击手理论”），因火箭破裂处上方约200英尺，且附近有竞争对手的建筑。SpaceX进行了多次测试，并与联邦航空管理局（FAA）沟通，最终FAA确认不存在外部袭击，爆炸源于火箭上层氦气罐破裂。此次失败推动了SpaceX对火箭设计的改进。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：SpaceX火箭爆炸的原因及相关调查过程

不同观点：
• **khelavastr的观点**：火箭爆炸是由于SpaceX旧的ERP系统未能有效追踪零部件，尤其是未正确存储需要液氮的燃料罐。这导致了燃料罐出现裂缝，最终在加注液氧时发生爆炸。该评论还提到，事故后公司将质量 assurance ERP系统迁移到了新的ERP系统（Warp）。

• **vrosas的观点**：提到公司内的工程师和技术人员进行了一项有趣的实验，他们使用.50口径的枪射击加压氦气罐以观察是否会爆炸。这被描述为技术人员们工作中最有趣的一天。

• **Factory_Reset的观点**：详细描述了爆炸调查的过程，包括初期对内部故障的怀疑和长达10个月的调查。提到使用.50口径枪支进行实验，最终发现问题出在之前外包的某个火箭部件上，并因此建立了公司内部的供应链。这一改变后的部件在后续的试验中没有再出现问题。

• **jowea的观点**：提到自己读过的一本书，该书与这个真实事件有某种关联，但未详细说明具体内容。

• **scrubs的观点**：通过引述1970年代的电视节目情景，表达了对诸如马斯克等公众人物和相关事件的复杂感受，并质疑关于狙击手导致爆炸的猜测。

• **Polizeiposaune的观点**：将火箭爆炸比作汽车在车库中自燃的情况，提到某些老式福特汽车因巡航控制缺陷导致火灾的事件，并指出这类问题通常通过召回解决。

• **AnimalMuppet的观点**：认为如果观察到来自竞争对手建筑的闪光与爆炸时间吻合，那么调查狙击手理论是可以理解的，但不应在公开场合过多讨论，以免被认为是推卸责任。

• **7e的观点**：认为关于SpaceX爆炸事件的讨论是被埃隆·马斯克的偏执狂态度影响，并将这种情绪传递给了一些新手工程师。

补充讨论：
• 调查过程中涉及的实验和测试方法被一些评论者认为是有趣且必要的，尽管可能存在一定的危险性和不确定性。
• 关于狙击手导致爆炸的猜测虽然被部分讨论，但最终被认为是不可信或不重要的。
• 对ERP系统和供应链问题的讨论反映出技术管理和零部件追踪对航天项目的重要性。

争议焦点：
• 关于火箭爆炸的真正原因存在不同的推测和解释，部分讨论者认为公司可能试图通过外部因素转移责任。
• 对埃隆·马斯克及其公司文化的评价存在分歧，部分评论者对其管理和调查方式持怀疑态度。

The rocket was there. And then it decidedly was
not
.
Shortly after sunrise on a late summer morning nearly nine years ago at SpaceX's sole operational launch pad, engineers neared the end of a static fire test. These were still early days for their operation of a Falcon 9 rocket that used super-chilled liquid propellants, and engineers pressed to see how quickly they could complete fueling. This was because the liquid oxygen and kerosene fuel warmed quickly in Florida's sultry air, and cold propellants were essential to maximizing the rocket's performance.
On this morning, September 1, 2016, everything proceeded more or less nominally up until eight minutes before the ignition of the rocket's nine Merlin engines. It was a stable point in the countdown, so no one expected what happened next.
"I saw the first explosion," John Muratore, launch director for the mission, told me. "It came out of nowhere, and it was really violent. I swear, that explosion must have taken an hour. It felt like an hour. But it was only a few seconds. The second stage exploded in this huge ball of fire, and then the payload kind of teetered on top of the transporter erector. And then it took a swan dive off the top rails, dove down, and hit the ground. And then it exploded."
The dramatic loss of the Falcon 9 rocket and its Amos-6 satellite,
captured on video
by a commercial photographer, came at a pivotal moment for SpaceX and the broader commercial space industry. It was SpaceX's second rocket failure in a little more than a year, and it occurred as NASA was betting heavily on the company to carry its astronauts to orbit. SpaceX was not the behemoth it is today, a company valued at $350 billion. It remained vulnerable to the vicissitudes of the launch industry. This violent failure shook everyone, from the engineers in Florida to satellite launch customers to the suits at NASA headquarters in Washington, DC.
As part of my book on the Falcon 9 and Dragon years at SpaceX,
Reentry
, I reported deeply on the loss of the Amos-6 mission. In the weeks afterward, the greatest mystery was what had precipitated the accident. It was understood that a pressurized helium tank inside the upper stage had ruptured. But why? No major parts on the rocket were moving at the time of the failure. It was, for all intents and purposes, akin to an automobile idling in a driveway with half a tank of gasoline. And then it exploded.
This failure gave rise to one of the oddest—but also strangely compelling—stories of the 2010s in spaceflight. And we're still learning new things today.
The “sniper” theory
The lack of a concrete explanation for the failure led SpaceX engineers to pursue hundreds of theories. One was the possibility that an outside "sniper" had shot the rocket. This theory appealed to SpaceX founder Elon Musk, who was asleep at his home in California when the rocket exploded. Within hours of hearing about the failure, Musk gravitated toward the simple answer of a projectile being shot through the rocket.
This is not as crazy as it sounds, and other engineers at SpaceX aside from Musk entertained the possibility, as some circumstantial evidence to support the notion of an outside actor existed. Most notably, the first rupture in the rocket occurred about 200 feet above the ground, on the side of the vehicle facing the southwest. In this direction, about one mile away, lay a building leased by SpaceX's main competitor in launch, United Launch Alliance. A separate video indicated a flash on the roof of this building, now known as the Spaceflight Processing Operations Center. The timing of this flash matched the interval it would take a projectile to travel from the building to the rocket.
A sniper on the roof of a competitor's building—forget the
Right Stuff
, this was the stuff of a Mission: Impossible or James Bond movie.
At Musk's direction, SpaceX worked this theory both internally and externally. Within the company, engineers and technicians actually took pressurized tanks that stored helium—one of these had burst, leading to the explosion—and shot at them in Texas to determine whether they would explode and what the result looked like. Externally, they sent the site director for their Florida operations, Ricky Lim, to inquire whether he might visit the roof of the United Launch Alliance building.
SpaceX pursued the sniper theory for more than a month. A few SpaceX employees told me that they did not stop this line of inquiry until the Federal Aviation Administration sent the company a letter definitively saying that there was no gunman involved. It would be interesting to see this letter, so I submitted a Freedom of Information Act request to the FAA in the spring of 2023. Because the federal FOIA process moves slowly, I did not expect to receive a response in time for the book. But it was worth a try a
43894678.article_summary: 2016年9月1日，SpaceX在佛罗里达进行Falcon 9火箭静态点火测试时，火箭在发动机点火前意外爆炸，导致火箭及所载Amos-6卫星损毁。这起事故是SpaceX的第二次火箭失败，正值公司与NASA合作的关键时期，引发了广泛关注。由于没有立即找到明确原因，SpaceX内部甚至怀疑是否是外部袭击（“狙击手理论”），因火箭破裂处上方约200英尺，且附近有竞争对手的建筑。SpaceX进行了多次测试，并与联邦航空管理局（FAA）沟通，最终FAA确认不存在外部袭击，爆炸源于火箭上层氦气罐破裂。此次失败推动了SpaceX对火箭设计的改进。

不同观点：
• **khelavastr的观点**：火箭爆炸是由于SpaceX旧的ERP系统未能有效追踪零部件，尤其是未正确存储需要液氮的燃料罐。这导致了燃料罐出现裂缝，最终在加注液氧时发生爆炸。该评论还提到，事故后公司将质量 assurance ERP系统迁移到了新的ERP系统（Warp）。

• **vrosas的观点**：提到公司内的工程师和技术人员进行了一项有趣的实验，他们使用.50口径的枪射击加压氦气罐以观察是否会爆炸。这被描述为技术人员们工作中最有趣的一天。

• **Factory_Reset的观点**：详细描述了爆炸调查的过程，包括初期对内部故障的怀疑和长达10个月的调查。提到使用.50口径枪支进行实验，最终发现问题出在之前外包的某个火箭部件上，并因此建立了公司内部的供应链。这一改变后的部件在后续的试验中没有再出现问题。

data.title: Building a more accessible GitHub CLI
data.author: four_fifths
data.article_summary: GitHub致力于提升其工具对所有开发者的可访问性，包括GitHub CLI（命令行界面）。与网页不同，终端环境缺乏全面的无障碍标准，如WCAG。GitHub通过Public Preview版着力解决屏幕阅读器用户、高对比度需求用户及色彩定制需求用户的访问ibility问题。开发团队研究了辅助技术如何与终端交互，改进了提示和进度显示，使屏幕阅读器能准确传达信息，并优化了色彩与对比度设置。通过这些改进，GitHub CLI变得更加包容，适应不同用户的需求。用户可在最新版GitHub CLI中运行“gh a11y”启用这些功能。

43894259.article_content:
Ryan Hecht
&
Andrew Feller
May 2, 2025
|
7 minutes
Share:
At GitHub, we’re committed to making our tools truly accessible for every developer, regardless of ability or toolset. The command line interface (CLI) is a vital part of the developer experience, and the
GitHub CLI
is our product that brings the power of GitHub to your terminal.
When it comes to accessibility, the terminal is fundamentally different from a web browser or a graphical user interface, with a lineage that predates the web itself. While standards like the Web Content Accessibility Guidelines (WCAG) provide a clear path for making web and graphical applications accessible, there is no equivalent, comprehensive standard for the terminal and CLIs. The W3C offers
some high-level guidance for non-web software
, but it stops short of prescribing concrete techniques, leaving much open to interpretation and innovation.
This gap has challenged us to think creatively and purposefully about what accessibility should look like in the terminal. Our recent
Public Preview
is focused on addressing the needs of three key groups: users who rely on screen readers, users who need high contrast between background and text, and users who require customizable color options. Our work aims to make the GitHub CLI more inclusive for all, regardless of how you interact with your terminal. Run
gh a11y
in the latest version of the GitHub CLI to enable these features, or read on to learn about our path to designing and implementing them.
Understanding the terminal landscape
Text-based and command-line applications differ fundamentally from graphical or web applications. On a web page, assistive technologies like screen readers make use of the document object model (DOM) to infer structure and context of the page. Web pages can be designed such that the DOM’s structure is friendly to these technologies without impacting the visual design of the page.  By contrast, CLI’s primary output is plain text, without hidden markup. A terminal emulator acts as the “user agent” for text apps, rendering characters as directed by the server application. Assistive technologies access this matrix of characters, analyze its layout, and try to infer structure. As the
WCAG2ICT guidance
notes, accessibility in this space means ensuring that all text output is available to assistive technologies, and that structural information is conveyed in a way that’s programmatically determinable—even if no explicit markup is present.
In our quest to improve the GitHub CLI’s usability for blind, low-vision, and colorblind users, we found ourselves navigating a landscape with lots of guidance, but few concrete techniques for implementing accessible experiences. We studied how assistive technology interacts with terminals: how screen readers review output, how color and contrast can be customized, and how structural cues can be inferred from plain text. Our recent Public Preview contains explorations into various use cases in these spaces.
Rethinking prompts and progress for screen readers
One of the GitHub CLI’s strengths as a command-line application is its rich prompting experience, which gives our users an interactive interface to enter command options. However, this rich interactive experience poses a hurdle for speech synthesis screen readers: Non-alphanumeric visual cues and uses of constant screen redraws for visual or other effects can be tricky to correctly interpret as speech.
A demo video with sound of screen reader reading legacy prompter.
To reduce confusion and make it easier for blind and low vision users to confidently answer questions and navigate choices, we’re introducing a prompting experience that allows speech synthesis screen readers to accurately convey prompts to users. Our new prompter is built using Charm’s open source
charmbracelet/huh
prompting library
.
A demo of a screenreader correctly reading a prompt.
Another use case where the terminal is redrawn for visual effect is when showing progress bars. Our existing implementation uses a “spinner” made by redrawing the screen to display different braille characters (yes, we appreciate the irony) to give the user the indication that their command is executing. Speech synthesis screen readers do not handle this well:
A demo of a screenreader and an old spinner.
This has been replaced with a static text progress indicator (with a relevant message to the action being taken where possible, falling back to a general “Working…” message). We’re working on identifying other areas we can further improve the contextual text.
A demo video of the new progress indicator experience.
Color, contrast, and customization
Color is more than decoration in the terminal: It’s a vital tool for highlighting information, signaling errors, and guiding workflows. But color can also be a barrier—if contrast between the color of the terminal background and the text displayed on it is too low, some users will have difficulty discerning the displayed informa

data.title: Internet usage pattern during power outage in Spain and Portugal
data.author: ghoshbinayak
data.article_summary: 本文回顾了2025年4月28日伊比利亚半岛大停电期间的网络流量变化。通过对西班牙和葡萄牙的流量数据分析，发现停电期间两国的网络流量显著下降，尤其是中午至下午时段。停电始于葡萄牙上午11:33，随后蔓延至西班牙。尽管桌面流量急剧下降，移动流量却相对稳定，显示人们通过移动设备保持联网。停电初期，有线网络连接大幅减少，而移动网络和无线热点使用增加。人们在停电期间主要访问新闻和政府网站，以获取最新信息，同时关注食品安全的相关内容。西班牙和葡萄牙的流量模式略有不同，但总体趋势相似。

不同观点：

• codetrotter 描述了在瓦伦西亚经历的电力中断对其生活的影响，包括移动互联网不稳定、手机信号差、无法获取信息等问题。此外，他提到由于住在8楼且有一个1岁婴儿，上下楼梯非常不便，并且由于依赖电子支付而没有现金应对长时间的停电。

• giorgioz 表示自己在西班牙停电期间依然有3G数据连接，而一些邻居则没有信号。他推测可能是某些运营商有备用柴油发电机，维持了几个小时的网络服务。

• TrianguloY 提到在大学里由于备用发电机而迅速恢复了有线网络连接，而在家中大部分路由器停止工作，直到第二天才恢复正常。他还指出移动网络的拥堵问题，导致很多人无法连接互联网。

• myself248 和 NooneAtAll3 都对手机电池电量信息如何泄露给互联网表示好奇。

• whitehexagon 描述了电力恢复后移动电话服务依然延迟恢复的情况，并提到银行不处理现金以及ATM离线的问题。他还寻求有关便携式收音机的推荐，以便在未来类似事件中获取信息。

• wkat4242 指出在停电期间，即使是使用UPS系统的用户，固定电话互联网也很快中断，而5G网络完全不可用。所有三个主要网络都仅限于紧急通话状态，不允许数据传输。他还提到考虑过使用Starlink作为备份，但由于费用和政治因素而放弃。

• anthk 分享了在毕尔巴鄂经历的2G/3G连接问题，并通过使用Gopher和Gemini代理访问新闻。他还提到有些人购买了FM收音机接收器以获取应急信息。

• dukeofdoom 回忆了安大略多年前的一次长达7天的停电事件，认为这样的经历让人更接近自然和社区，并对现代技术依赖的生活方式提出反思。

• lopkeny12ko 提到Starlink在停电期间的使用量激增，并提供了一个相关的Twitter链接。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点主要集中在西班牙午餐时间和午休传统的准确性以及停电期间网络连接的实际状况。
• 讨论还涉及如何在停电和网络中断情况下有效获取信息和进行通信，包括使用备用发电机、FM收音机和可能的卫星互联网服务。
• 人们对现代技术依赖和在电力及网络中断时的应对措施表达了不同的看法和建议。

43894363.article_content:
A look back at the Iberian power outage of April 28
By
Philip Tellis
on
03 May 2025
Table of Contents
Overall traffic
Identifying the Anomaly
Drilling into the details
How long could it last?
In closing
On Monday, April 28, the
Iberian Peninsula suffered a major power outage
that
disabled many services
across these countries.  In this post I'll look at the patterns we saw in
mPulse data during this time.
Overall traffic
I first looked at the overall data patterns for traffic originating from Spain & Portugal for several weeks prior to the outage.
While
other regions
were also
slightly affected
, these two countries
suffered the worst of it.
The image above shows traffic patterns for these two countries for 7 days around the event at 1 hour granularity. We see that on average (in that mode I mean the medians),
Spain has about 4.5 times the traffic of Portugal. This is expected, since Spain's population (48m) is 4.5 times that of Portugal (10.5).
Identifying the Anomaly
I then ran mPulse's Anomaly Detection against this data.
The Anomaly Detection logic shows that traffic dropped below expected levels between 12pm & 1pm
CEST
(local time in Madrid),
and then returned to normal sometime around 2am on the 29th.  This chart only shows traffic from Spain, but you get the picture.
Drilling into the details
I then looked at the data at finer granularity. This time at 5 minute intervals comparing April 28th to the week prior. Ideally I'd have used the previous Monday, but as that
was the Easter Monday holiday, the traffic patterns were unusual on that day as well. I settled on Wednesday, April 23rd as a representative day for the prior week. Just to be
sure, I also looked at data from France & Germany to make sure we weren't seeing a common change in pattern.
Also, to be clear, for any of the following charts that refer to a single country, the time axis will be in that country's time zone. This means that Portugal shows up in
WEST
rather than
CEST
.
The outage started at 11:33am in Portugal which is 12:33pm in Spain.
I looked at several different dimensions, but the first one to stand out was Device Type.
Mobile Lunches
For all 4 countries that I looked at, there is a sharp drop in desktop traffic around lunch time. In France and Portugal desktop traffic drops from about 12-2pm with its trough
around 1pm.  In Germany the drop is between 12-1pm while in Spain it starts around 1pm, and goes until 4 or 5pm. The drop in Spain is less steep than that in France & Portugal
suggesting that it's more staggerred across this 3-4 hour period rather than all at once.
During this afternoon break, we see traffic moving to mobile devices.
During the outage
At the start of the power outage, we notice that while traffic drops 80% on desktop, there is only a 40% drop on mobile. At this time, and going on for a few hours,
there is more mobile traffic than desktop traffic. In fact mobile traffic remains higher than desktop traffic until the next morning, but this appears to be a common
pattern where traffic typically moves to mobile as people leave work around 5pm.
I was curious about that intial part of the outage. If there wasn't power, then how were people still connecting to the Internet? Naturally their phones still had sufficient
battery power, but were there cell phone signals or other networks that were usable?
Connection sources
For these charts I looked only at mobile devices to see how they were connecting to the Internet.
For both Spain & Portugal, we see that Wired connections (this includes WiFi you may have at home, the office or a coffee shop since it uses
NAT
over a wire, but not ISP provided WiFi networks where you get a public IP over WiFi) drop off significantly. There's about a 50 percentage point drop in wired traffic. At
the same time, Portugal saw a 30 percentage point increase in Cellular network usage. There were even a few wireless hotspots that appear at this time.
Destinations
What kinds of sites were most interesting at this time? What were people willing to use their limited electric reserves on? I grouped destination sites by Industry to
try and make some sense of it.
There are different patterns for Spain & Portugal, so I'll look at them separately.
Remember that in Portugal the outage started at 11:33am local time. Almost immediately we see an
increase
in traffic to news websites with people trying to find out
what was going on. There are also periodic updates on government websites that see an increase in traffic.
There's a drop in Retail, Entertainment and Financial activity.
There is also a sudden new stream of visits to sites dealing with Food Safety and the safe handling of food, possibly because people have to figure out what's safe to hold
on to without refrigeration.  I should mention that there were no visits to these sites at any time prior to this event for the several weeks that I looked at the data.
Food safety and Government websites seem to be common with Spain as well.
However Spanish us

• myself248 和 NooneAtAll3 都对手机电池电量信息如何泄露给互联网表示好奇。

• sillyfluke 对西班牙和葡萄牙人在欧盟其他地区漫游时的网络体验差异表示好奇，特别是通过本国电信公司连接时是否会有不同的体验。

• whitehexagon 描述了电力恢复后移动电话服务依然延迟恢复的情况，并提到银行不处理现金以及ATM离线的问题。他还寻求有关便携式收音机的推荐，以便在未来类似事件中获取信息。

• wkat4242 指出在停电期间，即使是使用UPS系统的用户，固定电话互联网也很快中断，而5G网络完全不可用。所有三个主要网络都仅限于紧急通话状态，不允许数据传输。他还提到考虑过使用Starlink作为备份，但由于费用和政治因素而放弃。

• anthk 分享了在毕尔巴鄂经历的2G/3G连接问题，并通过使用Gopher和Gemini代理访问新闻。他还提到有些人购买了FM收音机接收器以获取应急信息。

• dukeofdoom 回忆了安大略多年前的一次长达7天的停电事件，认为这样的经历让人更接近自然和社区，并对现代技术依赖的生活方式提出反思。

• lopkeny12ko 提到Starlink在停电期间的使用量激增，并提供了一个相关的Twitter链接。

• 争议焦点主要集中在西班牙午餐时间和午休传统的准确性以及停电期间网络连接的实际状况。
• 讨论还涉及如何在停电和网络中断情况下有效获取信息和进行通信，包括使用备用发电机、FM收音机和可能的卫星互联网服务。
• 人们对现代技术依赖和在电力及网络中断时的应对措施表达了不同的看法和建议。

data.title: Extending a Language – Writing Powerful Macros in Scheme
data.author: textread
data.article_summary:
本文介绍了如何在Scheme中编写强大的宏，重点讲解了Scheme宏系统的高级特性和应用。Scheme的宏机制因其内建的**卫生**特性而强大，能够创建与语言内置语法无缝结合的抽象。本文从简单宏示例入手，逐步讲解了**语法对象**、**syntax-case宏**、**打破卫生**的方法、**阶段**（phasing）概念及其实现、以及**扩展**如别名和语法参数等。文章还提供了**复杂示例**，如用宏实现LR(1)解析器生成器，并附有练习。本文旨在让读者了解Scheme宏的表达力，并鼓励语言设计者在语言中加入类似机制。

**前提条件**包括使用Chez Scheme、Emacs、Org、Geiser、Paredit等工具搭建开发环境，并提供了相关配置说明。

完整文档见：[HTML版本](https://mnieper.github.io/scheme-macros/README.html) 及 [Org文档](https://github.com/mnieper/scheme-macros)。

1.
Preface
This document is an introduction to writing powerful macros in Scheme.
It was initially written on the occasion of a tutorial I give at the
BOB2023 Konferenz
in Berlin on 17 March 2023.
The macro facility, especially its built-in
hygiene
, is one of the
fundamental pillars of the Scheme programming language.  While more
complicated than the simple token-replacing macros of other languages
like C, Scheme macros can be written in a way that make them robust
and so that the abstractions they offer seamless blend into the
language and cannot be distinguished from syntactic forms built into
the language.  It is often felt that this expressiveness makes writing
Scheme macros more complicated (even something of a black art) than
writing C or Common Lisp macros, for example.  One goal of this
tutorial is to convince the audience otherwise.
While the Scheme macro facility has always been avant-garde (and this
is one of the reasons why Scheme was chosen as the implementation
language for this tutorial), a lot of what is said here also applies
to languages that provide corresponding features.  It is also a appeal
to language designers that languages should include a macro facility
as Scheme does, as this allows for small language cores and enables
the user to provide their own syntactic abstractions.
Another reason why the Scheme language is used in this tutorial is
that it has an exceptionally clear semantics, is a compact language,
and is easy to learn.
The document can both be read as is or used interactively in an Emacs
session.  In the following section, a possible setup is described.
2.
Prerequisites
2.1.
Chez Scheme
We need a Scheme implementation.  This tutorial assumes
Chez Scheme
,
which is one of the most mature, standard-compliant Scheme
implementations.  You can get Chez Scheme from its homepage.  On
Debian-based GNU/Linux system like Ubuntu, it is prepackaged.
2.2.
Emacs
We will use
GNU Emacs
as our development environment, which has great
tooling for Scheme.  The typical GNU/Linux system ships with it.
For GNU Emacs < 28, enable the
NonGNU Emacs Lisp Package Archive
in
your
init file
or
customize
the variable
package-archives
.
Likewise, enable the
NonGNU-devel ELPA Packages
.
2.3.
Org
Org Mode
is a GNU Emacs major mode that allows to document, edit and
execute source code.
The current versions of Org packaged with Emacs hide Scheme evaluation
errors.  This is fixed in the version in Org's git repository, for
which Org
provides installation instructions
.
Familiarize yourself with how one works with
source code in an Org
document
, especially how to
edit
and
execute code
.
2.4.
Geiser
Geiser
is a GNU Emacs package that allows to runs Scheme processes in
GNU Emacs, and which is used by Org's Babel.  To install it, it is
enough to install the package
geiser-chez
using GNU Emacs'
package
menu
.  We need the most recent development version.
2.5.
Paredit
Paredit
, a tool for parenthetical editing in Emacs makes working with
Scheme code a lot more pleasant.  Like Geiser, it can be installed
through GNU Emacs' package manager.

主要讨论点：关于不同微处理器和DOS仿真软件的性能及使用体验的评论

不同观点：
• 观点一：强调80x86系列微处理器相关的经典书籍，包括对8086、80286、80386以及386、486和Pentium等处理器的深入介绍。这表明评论者对历史上的微处理器技术及其文献有深入的了解和兴趣。

• 观点二：支持DOSEmu作为DOS仿真工具，认为其性能优于DOSBox。具体提到DOSEmu运行DOS（如FreeDOS、DRDOS和MSDOS）时速度更快，更接近于Wine而不是完全仿真，并且具有DPMI设置。这显示出评论者对DOSEmu的技术优势有明确的支持态度。

• 观点三：通过具体例子（如DN3D的运行表现）说明DOSEmu在实际应用中的优越性，尤其是在实时运行方面比DOSBox表现更好。这进一步强化了对DOSEmu性能的肯定。

补充讨论：
- 评论中提到了DOSEmu和DOSBox在运行DOS程序时的性能对比，这是讨论的技术核心。
- 评论者通过具体的技术细节（如DPMI设置和实时运行表现）来支持自己的观点，提供了具体的论据。
- 争议的焦点可能在于DOSEmu和DOSBox各自的优劣，特别是在不同硬件和应用场景下的表现差异。

总结来看，评论主要围绕微处理器相关书籍的推荐以及DOS仿真软件的性能对比展开，其中对DOSEmu的技术优势有较强的偏向性。

data.article_summary: 新西兰惠灵顿机场将移除以《霍比特人》为主题的巨型鹰雕，这些鹰雕自2013年《霍比特人》三部曲上映时安装，已成为机场标志。鹰雕由维塔工作室制作，每只重1.2吨，翼展15米，内部为钢骨架，外部为聚苯乙烯。尽管鹰雕深受欢迎，但将为新的神秘展品让路，并被存放，尚无长期计划。机场CEO马特·克拉克表示，正与维塔工作室合作设计新的本地主题替代品，今年晚些时候揭晓。2014年，其中一只鹰雕在地震中坠落，无人受伤。不过，霍比特主题的巨龙史矛革雕塑将继续在值机区展示。

NZ airport to remove Hobbit-themed eagle sculptures
9 hours ago
Share
Save
Koh Ewe
BBC News
Share
Save
Wellington Airport
The giant birds will be unfastened from the airport ceiling to make way for a new mystery exhibit
For more than a decade, a pair of Hobbit-inspired eagle sculptures have cast a watchful eye over visitors at New Zealand's Wellington Airport.
But the giant birds will be unfastened from the ceiling on Friday to make way for a new mystery exhibit, airport authorities said.
The eagles appear as messengers in JRR Tolkien's The Lord of the Rings and The Hobbit, which were adapted to film by New Zealand's Sir Peter Jackson.
The spectacular New Zealand landscapes featured in Mr Jackson's films are a consistent draw for tourists, who are greeted at the airport by the eagle sculptures.
"It's not unusual to see airborne departures from Wellington Airport, but in this case, it will be emotional for us," Wellington Airport chief executive Matt Clarke said in a statement.
The giant eagles will be placed in storage and there have not been long-term plans for them.
Each eagle weighs 1.2 tonnes (1,200kg) with a wingspan of 15m (49ft). Riding on the back of one of the birds is a sculpture of the wizard, Gandalf.
Made of polystyrene and with an internal steel skeleton, each eagle has hundreds of feathers, the longest one measuring 2.4m (8ft).
While the iconic eagles will soon be gone, not all is lost for fans of the franchise: Smaug the Magnificent, the dragon in The Hobbit, will continue to be displayed at the check-in area.
Wellington Airport
The sculptures were installed in 2013 amid the release of The Hobbit trilogy
The eagles were unveiled in 2013, around the time of the release of The Hobbit trilogy. The giant sculptures were produced by Wētā Workshop, the New Zealand-based company that made costumes and props for The Lord of the Rings franchise.
"We're working with Wētā Workshop on some exciting plans for a unique, locally themed replacement to take their place," Mr Clarke said. "We'll unveil what's next later this year so keep watching the skies."
In 2014, one of the eagles came crashing down during an earthquake. No one was injured from that accident.

data.article_summary: 这篇文章讲述了作者通过一次偶然的发现，意识到学校午餐债务问题对孩子们的羞辱和影响。作者了解到犹他州学校午餐债务总计280万美元，个别小学的债务甚至只有835美元，但这笔小额资金却能避免许多孩子在公共场合感到羞愧。作者决定自己支付了一些债务，并开始关注更多学校的债务情况。文章揭示了学校午餐债务背后隐藏的儿童贫困问题，以及社会对这一问题的忽视。作者呼吁人们关注这一现象，并通过实际行动帮助减轻受影响家庭的负担。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：美国公立学校学生的免费午餐问题，包括午餐债务、资助机制和普遍免费午餐的可行性。

不同观点：
• thinkingtoilet：指出目前资助机制存在“一刀切”的问题，建议采用梯度资助方式，以避免因刚性界限造成的困境。同时提到残疾人士的资助也面临类似问题。
• M3L0NM4N：质疑现行免费午餐资格审查的管理成本，认为直接给所有学生提供免费午餐可能更简单有效。
• mproud：赞赏明尼苏达州的免费午餐计划，并乐见其他州开始实施类似政策。
• labrador：分享个人经历，说明在某些州，午餐债务可能导致食物羞辱，而在其他州则没有这种问题。
• rpcope1：认为一个繁荣的国家应为所有需要的儿童提供三餐，质疑为何美国尚未实现这一点。
• andreicap：来自摩尔多瓦的评论者分享自己国家也开始实施免费午餐，并质疑为何美国尚未在联邦层面推行。
• pragmatic：指出有些家庭因为语言障碍、自尊或官僚程序复杂而不申请免费午餐，认为无条件提供午餐是社会应做的事情。
• phkahler：同意短期和长期解决方案应同时进行，避免因债务解决而忽视结构性改革。
• dataflow：对午餐债务的运作机制感到困惑，质疑即使还清债务，是否问题仍会反复出现。
• airstrike：认为文章感人，并感谢分享相关信息。
• neilv：分享个人经历，认为不应通过让儿童经历“性格塑造”来接受阶级不平等，主张直接提供儿童所需的基本照顾。
• klntsky：认为美国文化受罪恶感驱动，但在财务上采用羞耻感控制机制，可能与宗教影响减弱有关。
• msravi：询问美国学校是否为不同学生提供不同餐食，以及决定标准是什么。
• ItsBob：分享苏格兰所有小学生均可享受免费午餐的体验，认为不应将午餐债务问题转嫁给儿童。

补充讨论：
• 讨论焦点集中在现行午餐资助机制的公平性和效率问题，以及普遍免费午餐的可行性。
• 有人提出梯度资助方案以解决刚性界限问题，而其他人则认为直接提供免费午餐更为简单有效。
• 个人经历和国际比较被用来支持普遍免费午餐的论点，强调不应让儿童因午餐债务受到影响。
• 有人质疑午餐债务问题的根源，认为这是成人设计的问题，不应影响儿童的基本需求。
• 对午餐债务的运作机制存在困惑，需要更清晰的解释。

43885101.article_content:
The thing about witnessing a 7-year-old having their hot lunch tray yanked away and replaced with a cold sandwich — what cafeteria workers in the biz euphemistically call an “alternative meal” — is not just the obvious cruelty of the public spectacle, though there’s plenty of that.
It’s the bizarre normalization of the whole affair, as if we’ve collectively agreed that fiscal responsibility is best taught through the ritual humiliation of second graders. It’s watching the adults in the room — ordinary, decent people who’d never dream of snatching food from a child in any other context — perform this strange ceremony with the mechanical resignation of DMV employees, while around them life continues uninterrupted, because this is just How Things Are.
I never actually witnessed this scene myself, but I’ve interviewed enough lunch ladies, principals and kids to construct a sort of composite mental image that now plays on an endless loop between my ears. It’s become my own personal film of educational injustice, frame by frame, in high-definition slow motion: the momentary confusion on the child’s face, the hushed explanation from the cashier, the sudden understanding dawning in the kid’s eyes, the burning shame that follows.
Advertisement
It’s the kind of thing most adults have trained themselves not to see, which is how I managed to live 29 years without recognizing an entire shadow economy of grade-school debt operating in the fluorescent-lit cafeterias of Utah, where I live. The invisibility of it all seems almost by design — a sleight-of-hand that kept this particular form of childhood poverty comfortably out of my peripheral vision until an algorithm decided I needed to know about it.
I was doomscrolling through news articles one evening — this was June 2024, which feels simultaneously like yesterday and several epochs ago — when I saw a headline stating there was $2.8 million in school lunch debt across Utah.
Advertisement
That seemed, you know, bad.
But it also triggered that now-familiar mental reflex where I immediately wondered if this was real or just another informational phantom conjured by our collective digital hallucination machine.
Advertisement
So I called my local school district, because that seemed like the sort of practical thing a reasonably civic-minded adult might do. I had no particular plan beyond basic verification. The woman who answered sounded simultaneously surprised and unsurprised that someone would call about this, if that makes sense. Yes, lunch debt was real, she told me. Yes, it affected children in our district. Yes, it was about $88,000
just for elementary schools
,
just in my district
. And then, almost as an afterthought, she mentioned that Bluffdale Elementary — a school I had no personal connection to — had about $835 in outstanding lunch debt.
$835.
The figure hit me like one of those rare moments of absolute clarity, utterly devoid of irony or ambiguity. Eight hundred and thirty-five dollars was the cost of preventing dozens of children from experiencing that moment of public shame I couldn’t stop imagining. It was less than some monthly car payments. It was approximately what I had spent the previous month on DoorDash and impulse Amazon purchases. The grotesque disproportion between the trivial financial sum and the profound human consequence felt like a cosmic accounting error.
“Can I just... pay that?” I asked, half expecting to be told about some bureaucratic impossibility.
“Um, sure,” she said. “Let me transfer you.”
Two days later, I drove to the district office during my lunch break from work and handed them a check. The entire process took approximately 11 minutes, during which I felt a disorienting mix of emotions: satisfaction at the immediate resolution, embarrassment at how easy it had been for me, and something more complicated — a dawning awareness of my own complicity in a system I hadn’t bothered to notice until now.
Advertisement
I wish I could tell you that I immediately founded a nonprofit, that I possessed some cinematic moment of purpose where an orchestral score swelled beneath my newfound determination. The truth is considerably less Hollywood-ready. I went back to work, coached my basketball team that evening, made dinner for my daughter, and didn’t think about it again for nearly two weeks.
What brought me back was the number: $2.8 million. It’s such a staggering figure. There’s more to the story than change lost between the couch cushions — families aren’t forgetting $2.8 million in lunch debt. People are suffering.
So, I called another district. Then another. I started a spreadsheet, which is what middle-class professionals do when faced with systemic problems — we quantify things, as if converting human suffering into Excel cells might render it more manageable. I learned that some elementary schools had thousands in debt. I learned that, contrary to popular belief, most school lunch debt doesn’t come from low-income families — those kids

data.title: Llama-Nemotron: Efficient Reasoning Models
data.author: nkko
data.article_summary: 文章介绍了一系列名为Llama-Nemotron的模型，这些模型具备高效的推理能力、推断效率和开放的企业使用许可。该系列包括三种规模：Nano（80亿参数）、Super（490亿参数）和Ultra（2530亿参数），在性能上可与最先进的推理模型（如DeepSeek-R1）竞争，同时提供更高的推断吞吐量和内存效率。模型的训练过程包括使用神经架构搜索、知识蒸馏、持续预训练以及由监督微调和大规模强化学习组成的推理聚焦后训练阶段。Llama-Nemotron模型是首个支持动态推理切换的开源模型，允许用户在推理过程中切换标准聊天和推理模式。为支持开放研究，作者还发布了模型、后训练数据集以及训练代码库。

Abstract:
We introduce the Llama-Nemotron series of models, an open family of heterogeneous reasoning models that deliver exceptional reasoning capabilities, inference efficiency, and an open license for enterprise use. The family comes in three sizes -- Nano (8B), Super (49B), and Ultra (253B) -- and performs competitively with state-of-the-art reasoning models such as DeepSeek-R1 while offering superior inference throughput and memory efficiency. In this report, we discuss the training procedure for these models, which entails using neural architecture search from Llama 3 models for accelerated inference, knowledge distillation, and continued pretraining, followed by a reasoning-focused post-training stage consisting of two main parts: supervised fine-tuning and large scale reinforcement learning. Llama-Nemotron models are the first open-source models to support a dynamic reasoning toggle, allowing users to switch between standard chat and reasoning modes during inference. To further support open research and facilitate model development, we provide the following resources: 1. We release the Llama-Nemotron reasoning models -- LN-Nano, LN-Super, and LN-Ultra -- under the commercially permissive NVIDIA Open Model License Agreement. 2. We release the complete post-training dataset: Llama-Nemotron-Post-Training-Dataset. 3. We also release our training codebases: NeMo, NeMo-Aligner, and Megatron-LM.

data.title: U.S. State Autism Databases
data.author: bookofjoe
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了美国一些州强制要求的自闭症注册数据库的伦理问题，以及心理学家Amy Marschall和其所在的Resiliency Mental Health机构在这些州的自闭症评估政策。由于认为将客户信息列入政府数据库是不道德的，Marschall医生不在有强制注册要求的州提供自闭症评估服务。例如，在北达科他州和印第安纳州，由于法律要求将所有自闭症患者注册，她拒绝提供评估服务。而在其他如特拉华州和新泽西州，她只为成年人（分别18岁和22岁以上）提供评估，因为这些年龄段的人不需注册。罗德岛的情况较为特殊，6岁以上个体不需强制注册，因此她在该州为6岁及以上的人提供评估服务。Marschall医生强调其政策会随法律变化调整，并会在客户要求时提供其他州的推荐服务。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：隐私保护措施是否能有效防止种族灭绝和国家支持的歧视，以及其对组织运作的影响。

不同观点：
• 观点一：隐私保护措施无法有效防止种族灭绝或国家支持的歧视。持此观点的人认为，这类 metrics（指标）可以通过其他多种途径获取，比如搜索历史、社交媒体行为、社交网络等，因此单独强调隐私保护并不能起到决定性作用。[concerndc1tizen]

• 观点二：隐私保护措施可能会妨碍善意组织的正常运作。该观点指出，过度的隐私保护可能会限制那些出于善意、试图保护人权的组织的行动能力，从而产生负面影响。[concerndc1tizen]

补充讨论：
• 隐私保护的局限性：有观点指出，即使加强隐私保护，政府或其他机构仍可能通过其他途径获取相关信息，因此质疑隐私保护的实际效果。

• 隐私保护与公共利益的平衡：评论中隐含了对隐私保护和公共利益之间如何平衡的讨论，即如何在保护个人隐私的同时，确保不会妨碍到对抗歧视和保护人权的努力。

争议焦点：
隐私保护措施是否能够有效防止种族灭绝和国家支持的歧视，以及在实施这些措施时，如何平衡对组织运作的影响。

43894301.article_content:
I have written before about my decision not to offer
autism evaluations in North Dakota
because of a state law that requires me to put my clients on a government list, which is unethical. In my research of North Dakota’s database, I learned that other states have similar registries with varying levels of ethical concern. My work has primarily focused on North Dakota because I am licensed to practice there, but now that I am a
PsyPact provider
, I need to be aware of these laws in all the states where I will practice.
This article reviews each autism database in the United States that I am aware of. I will provide my thoughts as a psychologist on the ethics of each state’s approach to the registries as well as Resiliency Mental Health’s policy on conducting autism evaluations in these states.
Photo by Tara Winstead on
Pexels.com
Please note that this article only focuses on states with mandatory registries. Some states have autism registries that are opt-in, meaning that the client can choose to consent to their inclusion. In states where registration is optional, it is my policy not to participate, and I do offer autism evaluations in those states if I am permitted to practice there. In the event that a client wants to opt in, I am happy to discuss their decision with them, but they will have to provide the information to the registry themselves.
All seven states that have mandatory autism registries are currently enrolled in PsyPact. More information about the various autism registries in the United States can be found in
this paper
. (Please be aware that this paper does not use neurodiversity-affirming language, though some of the information provided is useful.)
Note that, since this paper was published, New Hampshire eliminated their mandatory autism registry! Thank you, New Hampshire! Other states, please follow their example.
Disclaimer:
My policies around autism evaluations are subject to change as laws change and as I learn new information. Dr. Amy Marschall and Resiliency Mental Health reserve the right to decline to provide services that require Dr. Marschall to violate the ethics code of the American Psychological Association. If a client wants to seek an autism evaluation knowing they will be included in the registry, Dr. Marschall will provide referrals upon request to practitioners who conduct these evaluations in your state.
Delaware
Delaware requires that any provider who diagnoses autism in a child (under the age of 18) register the child with the state registry. In the past, the state has reviewed medical records due to suspicion that providers were not complying with the registry. At this time, the registry reportedly lacks funding, so it is unclear if it is still being updated. However, as written, Delaware law requires providers to register clients under age 18 with the state.
Dr. Amy Marschall and Resiliency Mental Health offer autism evaluations for adults age 18 or older in the state of Delaware because these individuals are not reported to the state autism registry.
Indiana
The state of Indiana originally only required registering autistic clients younger than age five, but in 2014 the law was updated to mandate registering any autistic client of any age. If a diagnosis is indicated in a hospital record, this information is automatically shared with the state.
Dr. Amy Marschall and Resiliency Mental Health do
not
offer autism evaluations to any individuals in the state of Indiana.
New Jersey
The autism registry in New Jersey requires that providers register clients diagnosed as autistic if the client has not yet reached their twenty-second birthday because the registry is run by the Division of Family Health Services, which provides case management only through age 21. New Jersey collects identifying information about autistic clients.
Dr. Amy Marschall and Resiliency Mental Health offer autism evaluations for adults age 22 or older in the state of New Jersey because these individuals are not included in the state autism registry.
North Dakota
North Dakota requires that all autistic individuals be registered with the state, regardless of age. Data collected includes identifying and contact information for autistic clients, information about family members, and additional information about the client’s medical and mental health history.
Dr. Amy Marschall and Resiliency Mental Health do
not
offer autism evaluations to any individuals in the state of North Dakota.
Rhode Island
Rhode Island has two autism registries. One requires that all clients age five and under be reported to the Birth Defects Registry. The second registry is for individuals age six to 21, and participation in the registry is voluntary.
Dr. Amy Marschall and Resiliency Mental Health offer autism evaluations to individuals ages six and older in the state of Rhode Island because registration of individuals ages six and up is not mandatory. Dr. Marschall does
not
register clients with the voluntary registry.

data.title: Carmakers Are Embracing Physical Buttons Again
data.author: ecliptik
data.article_summary: 从2024年开始，欧洲的碰撞测试组织EuroNCAP将鼓励汽车制造商使用物理按钮和控制装置，以提高车辆安全性。当前，许多汽车将关键控制功能隐藏在触摸屏菜单中，迫使驾驶员低头操作，增加事故风险。EuroNCAP要求基本功能如雨刷、转向灯和危险警示灯应通过物理控制实现，而非数字操作。一些厂商如大众已宣布在新车型中恢复使用物理按钮。尽管触摸屏设计在视觉上更简洁，但大多数司机仍偏好传统的物理按钮和旋钮。专家指出，触摸屏减少了驾驶的直觉性和安全性，因为它们缺乏触觉反馈，需要视觉和认知参与。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：汽车触屏控制与物理按钮的用户体验和安全性

不同观点：

Automakers that nest
key controls deep in touchscreen menus—forcing motorists to drive eyes-down rather than concentrate on the road ahead—may have their non-US safety ratings clipped next year.
From January, Europe’s crash-testing organization EuroNCAP, or New Car Assessment Program, will incentivize automakers to fit physical, easy-to-use, and tactile controls to achieve the highest safety ratings. “Manufacturers are on notice,” EuroNCAP’s director of strategic development Matthew Avery tells WIRED, “they’ve got to bring back buttons.”
Motorists, urges
EuroNCAP’s new guidance
, should not have to swipe, jab, or toggle while in motion. Instead, basic controls—such as wipers, indicators, and hazard lights—ought to be activated through analog means rather than digital.
Driving is one of the most
cerebrally challenging things humans manage
regularly—yet in recent years manufacturers seem almost addicted to switch-free, touchscreen-laden cockpits that, while pleasing to those keen on minimalistic design, are devoid of physical feedback and thus demand visual interaction, sometimes at the precise moment when eyes should be fixed on the road.
A smattering of automakers are slowly admitting that some smart screens are dumb. Last month, Volkswagen design chief Andreas Mindt said that next-gen models from the German automaker would get physical buttons for volume, seat heating, fan controls, and hazard lights. This shift will apply “in every car that we make from now on,”
Mindt told
British car magazine
Autocar
.
Acknowledging the touchscreen snafus by his predecessors—in 2019,
VW described
the “digitalized” Golf Mk8 as “intuitive to operate” and “progressive” when it was neither—Mindt said, “we will never, ever make this mistake anymore … It’s not a phone, it’s a car.”
Still, “the lack of physical switchgear is a shame” is now a common refrain in automotive reviews, including
on WIRED
. However, a limited but growing number of other automakers are dialing back the digital to greater or lesser degrees. The latest version of
Mazda’s CX-60 crossover SUV
features a 12.3-inch infotainment screen, but there’s still physical switchgear for operating the heater, air-con, and heated/cooled seats. While it’s still touch-sensitive, Mazda’s screen limits what you can prod depending on the app you’re using and whether you’re in motion. There’s also a real click wheel.
But many other automakers keep their touchscreen/slider/haptic/LLM doohickeys. Ninety-seven percent of new cars released after 2023 contain at least one screen,
reckons S&P Global Mobility
. Yet research last year by Britain’s
What Car?
magazine found that the vast majority of motorists prefer dials and switches to touchscreens. A survey of 1,428 drivers found that 89 percent preferred physical buttons.
Motorists, it seems, would much prefer to place their driving gloves in a glove compartment that opens with a satisfying IRL prod on a gloriously yielding and clicking clasp, rather than diving into a digital submenu. Indeed, there are several YouTube tutorials on how to open a Tesla’s glove box. “First thing,”
starts one
, “is you’re going to click on that car icon to access the menu settings, and from there on, you’re going to go to controls, and right here is the option to open your glove box.” As
Ronald Reagan wrote
, “If you’re explaining, you’re losing.”
Voice Control Reversion
The mass psychosis to fit digital cockpits is partly explained by economics—updatable touchscreens are cheaper to fit than buttons and their switchgear—but “there’s also a natural tendency [among designers] to make things more complex than they need to be,” argues Steven Kyffin, a former dean of design and pro vice-chancellor at Northumbria University in the UK (the alma mater of
button-obsessed Sir Jonny Ive
).
“Creating and then controlling complexity is a sign of human power,” Kyffin says. “Some people are absolutely desperate to have the flashiest, most minimalist, most post-modern-looking car, even if it is unsafe to drive because of all the distractions.”
Automakers shouldn’t encourage such consumers. “It is really important that steering, acceleration, braking, gear shifting, lights, wipers, all that stuff which enables you to actually drive the car, should be tactile,” says Kyffin, who once worked on smart controls for Dutch electronics company Philips. “From an interaction design perspective, the shift to touchscreens strips away the natural affordances that made driving intuitive,” he says.
“Traditional buttons, dials, and levers had perceptible and actionable qualities—you could feel for them, adjust them without looking, and rely on muscle memory. A touchscreen obliterates this," says Kyffin. "Now, you must look, think, and aim to adjust the temperature

data.title: How are cyber criminals rolling in 2025?
data.author: vin10
data.article_summary: 本文讨论了利用免费内容托管平台（如政府网站、大学和学校服务器）进行网络攻击的现象。这些本应安全的机构因网络安全措施不足，成为不法分子托管恶意内容的目标。攻击者通过过时的WordPress插件、缓存中毒、凭据填充和子域接管等手段入侵网站。他们并非直接植入恶意软件，而是通过一系列链接将用户引导至 affiliate 网络，从中获利，尤其针对寻找免费游戏货币"Robux"的儿童进行钓鱼攻击。尽管企业安全工具和防病毒软件常未能检测到这些链接，但攻击者仍擅长搜索引擎优化以绕过安全措施。文章还提到，早在2020年就有类似攻击事件发生，显示此问题并非新近出现。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：网络安全、诈骗手段、系统漏洞及维护问题

不同观点：
• **fckgw**：指出诈骗者利用支持网站的搜索功能和Google广告，将用户引导至诈骗电话。例如通过在Ticketmaster和Facebook的支持页面进行特定搜索并购买Google广告，使得诈骗链接看似合法。此方法利用了搜索引擎优化的漏洞，使用户难以分辨真伪。

• **SoftTalker**：讨论了过时的WordPress插件和CMS系统带来的安全隐患，特别是大学项目中由于资金和人员变动导致服务器无人维护的问题。虽然现在大学加强了管理，要求使用集中管理的企业CMS，但这一现象依然存在。

• **leftcenterright**：提到多种安全工具如Norton、Kaspersky等未能检测到这些诈骗链接，质疑这些工具在合规性检查中的有效性，认为其维护成本高且效果不佳。

• **gitroom**：支持SoftTalker的观点，分享了自己见过旧服务器因学生离开而无人管理，最终成为安全漏洞的经历。

• **ValdikSS**：讲述了自己通过特定搜索找到政府网站（*.gov.br）上的网络外壳（webshell）的经历，暗示政府网站也存在严重的安全漏洞。

• **3abiton**：提到自己发现了一些漏洞但因涉及不友好的机构而无法披露具体细节，有些漏洞即使报告后修复，相关方也未给予透明反馈，甚至有一次接到令人不安的电话。

• **mhuffman**：建议使用LLMs（大型语言模型）来检查诈骗邮件的拼写和语法，以制作更精致的诈骗页面，继续诈骗老年人的钱财。

• **wood_spirit**：对mhuffman提到的诈骗手段进行了简短的回应，询问是否涉及创建meme币等问题。

• **DyslexicAtheist**：通过具体Google搜索例子展示了如何在欧盟网站（europa.eu）上找到与流行文化相关的奇怪内容，暗示大型组织网站在内容管理和安全上的漏洞。

• **yapyap**：认为普通安全人员总是比最糟糕的网络罪犯慢一步，而国家支持的黑客则更为超前。尽管如此，仍认为这一现象从外部观察非常有趣。

• **superkuh**：认为当今大多数“网络”犯罪是由公司针对其客户/用户进行的，小型诈骗相比之下只是小巫见大巫。建议使用.html静态页面而非动态语言和数据库来减少安全漏洞。

• **Alex-Programs**：感觉近期的网络安全形势有所缓和，认为防守方逐渐占据上风，与几年前频繁出现的勒索软件和入侵事件相比，现在的情况有所改善。

补充讨论：
• 争议焦点在于安全工具的有效性和维护成本，以及在面对复杂多变的网络犯罪时，防守方是否能够跟上攻击方的步伐。
• 不同用户分享了实际经历和观察，强调了过时系统和无人维护服务器的安全隐患，并提出了一些可能的解决方案和改进建议。
• 讨论中也涉及了对大型组织和政府网站在安全管理上的质疑和实例分析。

How are they exploiting these sites?
I have been advised not to disclose specific vulnerabilities since the parties involved are not most friendly and transparent in handling security reports. While most of these got reported and some even got fixed, I can only disclose high-level details of the compromise path. Some just ghosted me after conveniently fixing the flaws, and one even gave me a phone call, which was somewhat scary and perhaps not worth the adrenaline.
Outdated Wordpress plugins and CMS systems
Cache poisoning via features like “search my site”
Credential stuffing
Dangling DNS records/ Subdomain takeovers
Why are they doing it?
Most of these files are not
malware
per se, since that might be a bit easy to detect out in the wild. But these PDFs and web pages link to a chain of websites. Each link would take the brave person who clicks them to another link and then to another, going through an affiliate network and making small amounts of money on the way.
Some of these links are also just plain phishing, mostly targeting kids looking for free/ cheap gaming gold “Robux”.
This is not new
I came across this post from July 2020 which discusses something similar:
https://medium.com/@thezedwards/july-2020-compromised-paf-subdomains-mostly-via-microsoft-azure-5834ae22733a
43896188.article_summary: 本文讨论了利用免费内容托管平台（如政府网站、大学和学校服务器）进行网络攻击的现象。这些本应安全的机构因网络安全措施不足，成为不法分子托管恶意内容的目标。攻击者通过过时的WordPress插件、缓存中毒、凭据填充和子域接管等手段入侵网站。他们并非直接植入恶意软件，而是通过一系列链接将用户引导至 affiliate 网络，从中获利，尤其针对寻找免费游戏货币"Robux"的儿童进行钓鱼攻击。尽管企业安全工具和防病毒软件常未能检测到这些链接，但攻击者仍擅长搜索引擎优化以绕过安全措施。文章还提到，早在2020年就有类似攻击事件发生，显示此问题并非新近出现。

data.article_summary: TextQuery是一款桌面应用，支持在macOS和Windows上使用，允许用户通过SQL导入、查询、修改和可视化数据。它无需定义 schema 或编写代码即可导入多种格式的数据文件，如Excel、CSV、JSON、ZIP等。应用提供强大的SQL编辑器，具有自动补全、查询历史、格式化等功能，并支持创建和自定义多种图表。此外，它还具备快速编辑数据、过滤、多标签页操作和数据导出等实用功能。TextQuery注重隐私和安全，不记录或发送任何用户数据，并提供一次性购买永久使用的许可。用户可以通过键盘快捷键提高效率，并可免费试用部分功能。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：Steampipe工具的应用、功能、潜在客户及技术实现

不同观点：
• **支持与祝贺**：
  - 多位用户（如[nathanwallace], [lowleveldesign]）对Steampipe的发布表示祝贺，认为这是一个有价值的工具，特别是在需要通过SQL查询多种服务和文件格式的场景下。
  
• **潜在客户与市场竞争**：
  - [bdcravens]指出，Steampipe面临的挑战是如何找到那些懂SQL但不愿意使用其他开源选项的客户，尤其是在受限环境中工作的数据分析师。
  - [dowager_dan99]表示自己已经是DuckDB的用户，不太可能购买Steampipe，但对市场潜力持开放态度，提到其他付费工具如Rider和DataGrip也有一定市场。

• **技术实现与功能建议**：
  - [ayhanfuat]对缺乏Parquet支持表示疑问，并建议使用DuckDB来实现该功能。
  - [A4ET8a8uTh0_v2]询问是否计划支持XML格式。
  - [moxplod]询问对大文件和多文件的处理能力，特别是针对2TB数据分布在700个CSV文件中的场景。
  - [jamroom]询问是否支持一次性导入多个文件，特别是ZIP文件中的CSV/XLSX文件。

• **替代方案与工具对比**：
  - [account-5]提到自己使用PowerShell或Nushell查询文件，也会使用SQLite。
  - [zipping1549]认为使用SQL的用户通常会将文件转换为正式的数据库，而不是使用类似Steampipe的工具。
  - [whoomp12342]提到以前通过SQL Server解决问题，暗示传统数据库工具也能满足类似需求。

补充讨论：
• **用户体验与技术问题**：
  - [flysand7]提到在Firefox浏览器上网站图片无法加载，并怀疑是HTTPS连接问题。
  - [imachine1980_]建议在页面上更清晰地说明购买选项，认为一次性购买和永久使用是一个很大的优势。
  - [hermitcrab]对“一次性购买，永久使用”的定价策略表示怀疑，认为未来可能会遇到问题。

• **技术栈选择**：
  - [snappr021]对使用Vanilla JS和HTML实现工具表示疑问，可能是在质疑当前技术选择。

争议焦点：
- Steampipe的市场定位与竞争优势，尤其是在已有许多开源和商业工具（如DuckDB、SQLite等）的情况下，如何吸引付费用户。
- 功能扩展与技术实现，特别是对Parquet支持和多文件导入等功能的需求。

data.title: As an experienced LLM user, I don't use generative LLMs often
data.author: minimaxir
data.article_summary:
文章主要讨论了作者作为BuzzFeed高级数据科学家，对生成型AI（特别是大型语言模型，LLM）的批判性看法及其实际应用经验。作者正在制定个人伦理声明，以阐明对现代生成型AI的立场，同时反思了自己在工作和个人项目中对LLM的利用，包括从早期的char-rnns到GPT-2、GPT-3以及ChatGPT的实验。

作者指出，虽然外界可能认为工程师频繁使用LLM，但实际上他并不常使用，且使用时需要根据具体情况进行调整。他强调了“提示工程”（prompt engineering）的重要性，尽管这一方法不被AI领域的人喜爱，但确实有效。作者避免使用ChatGPT.com等前端界面，而更偏好通过API访问LLM，如Anthropic的Claude API，因为这样可以更精细地控制生成规则、约束条件和“温度”参数，以减少AI的“幻觉”问题。

在专业工作中，作者通过LLM成功解决了一些实际问题，例如使用Claude API为BuzzFeed网站的大量文章自动分类。总体而言，作者认为尽管LLM有其局限性，但在特定应用中合理使用可以显著提高工作效率。
data.comments_summary:
主要讨论点：LLM（大型语言模型）在编程中的应用及其优缺点

不同观点：
• tptacek认为，LLM在处理代码任务时容易出现“幻觉”（hallucinate），即生成不存在的函数或方法，特别是当涉及到新库如polars时。他认为编码代理（coding agents）可以解决这一问题，因为它们可以通过迭代来修正错误，而无需用户深入文档查找。
• andy99指出，LLM在制作UI或网站模型方面具有价值，即使开发者缺乏前端经验，也可以快速生成可用于内部讨论的demo，而不适合实际部署。
• ziml77赞赏作者包含聊天记录，认为在做出关于LLM能力的声明时，提供证据支持是很重要的。
• simonw分享了使用LLM处理复杂代码问题的成功经验，特别是在使用较新的库时，通过搜索工具和将整个文档或代码库粘贴到提示中来提高准确性。
• behnamoh偏好使用LLM服务的“工作室”界面，而不是ChatGPT.com等前端界面，因为后者在模型控制和功能上受到限制，且有时模型表现不如预期。
• Jerry2询问是否需要自定义包装器来访问LLM API，或者是否有现成的客户端可以使用。
• Oras建议在需要返回一致的JSON时，定义一个JSON模式，以确保每次返回相同的结构，并提到在GPT-4o-mini上测试成功。
• qoez主要使用LLM来学习新知识和编写简单脚本，而不是依赖其一次性完成复杂任务。

• rfonseca引用了一个有趣的技巧，即让LLM扮演批评角色来改进自己的博客文章。
• geor9e对标题和内容的不一致表示不满，认为文章的“对抗性”框架削弱了实际的实用建议。
• Snuggly73对Claude改进代码时引入不必要的复杂性表示质疑。
• danbrooks作为数据科学家，认为提示工程对获得预期输出非常重要，特别是在快速周转的项目中。
• lxe认为文章的“与众不同”框架削弱了其实际有用的内容，并表示这种立场在技术讨论中令人厌倦。
• dukeofdoom分享了使用LLM开发pygame游戏的经验，指出LLM在处理复杂代码时容易出错，需要开发者密切监督和模块化设计。

补充讨论：
• LLM在处理新库和复杂代码时的局限性和潜在错误。
• 使用LLM生成UI/UX模型的实用性和价值。
• 不同LLM界面和工具在功能和控制上的差异。
• 提示工程和LLM输出质量之间的关系。
• LLM在实际开发中引入的复杂性和潜在的“复杂性陷阱”。

43897320.article_content:
Lately, I’ve been working on codifying a personal ethics statement about my stances on generative AI as I have been very critical about
several
aspects
of modern GenAI, and yet
I participate in it
. While working on that statement, I’ve been introspecting on how I myself have been utilizing large language models for both my professional work as a Senior Data Scientist at
BuzzFeed
and for my personal work blogging and
writing open-source software
. For about a decade, I’ve been researching and developing tooling around
text generation from char-rnns
, to the
ability to fine-tune GPT-2
, to
experiments with GPT-3
, and
even more experiments with ChatGPT
and other LLM APIs. Although I don’t claim to the best user of modern LLMs out there, I’ve had plenty of experience working against the cons of next-token predictor models and have become very good at finding the pros.
It turns out, to my surprise, that I don’t use them nearly as often as people think engineers do, but that doesn’t mean LLMs are useless for me. It’s a discussion that requires case-by-case nuance.
How I Interface With LLMs
#
Over the years I’ve utilized all the tricks to get the best results out of LLMs. The most famous trick is
prompt engineering
, or the art of phrasing the prompt in a specific manner to coach the model to generate a specific constrained output. Additions to prompts such as
offering financial incentives to the LLM
or simply
telling the LLM to make their output better
do indeed have a quantifiable positive impact on both improving adherence to the original prompt and the output text quality. Whenever my coworkers ask me why their LLM output is not what they expected, I suggest that they apply more prompt engineering and it almost always fixes their issues.
No one in the AI field is happy about prompt engineering
, especially myself. Attempts to remove the need for prompt engineering with more robust
RLHF
paradigms have only made it
even more rewarding
by allowing LLM developers to make use of better prompt adherence. True, “Prompt Engineer” as a job title
turned out to be a meme
but that’s mostly because prompt engineering is now an expected skill for anyone seriously using LLMs. Prompt engineering works, and part of being a professional is using what works even if it’s silly.
To that end,
I never use ChatGPT.com
or other normal-person frontends for accessing LLMs because they are harder to control. Instead, I typically access the backend UIs provided by each LLM service, which serve as a light wrapper over the API functionality which also makes it easy to port to code if necessary. Accessing LLM APIs like the ChatGPT API directly allow you to set
system prompts
which control the “rules” for the generation that can be very nuanced. Specifying specific constraints for the generated text such as “keep it to no more than 30 words” or “never use the word ‘delve’” tends to be more effective in the system prompt than putting them in the user prompt as you would with ChatGPT.com. Any modern LLM interface that does not let you explicitly set a system prompt is most likely
using their own system prompt
which you can’t control: for example, when ChatGPT.com had an issue where it was
too sycophantic
to its users, OpenAI
changed the system prompt
to command ChatGPT to “avoid ungrounded or sycophantic flattery.” I tend to use
Anthropic
Claude’s API — Claude Sonnet in particular — more than any ChatGPT variant because Claude anecdotally is less “robotic” and also handles coding questions much more accurately.
Additionally with the APIs, you can control the “
temperature
” of the generation, which at a high level controls the creativity of the generation. LLMs by default do not select the next token with the highest probability in order to allow it to give different outputs for each generation, so I prefer to set the temperature to
0.0
so that the output is mostly deterministic, or
0.2 - 0.3
if some light variance is required. Modern LLMs now use a default temperature of
1.0
, and I theorize that higher value is accentuating
LLM hallucination
issues where the text outputs are internally consistent but factually wrong.

VectorVFS: Your Filesystem as a Vector Database

VectorVFS: Your Filesystem as a Vector Database
¶
VectorVFS is a lightweight Python package that transforms your Linux filesystem into a vector database by
leveraging the native VFS (Virtual File System) extended attributes. Rather than maintaining a separate
index or external database, VectorVFS stores vector embeddings directly alongside each file—turning your
existing directory structure into an efficient and semantically searchable embedding store.
VectorVFS supports Meta’s Perception Encoders (PE)
[arxiv]
which
includes image/video encoders for vision language understanding, it outperforms InternVL3, Qwen2.5VL
and SigLIP2 for zero-shot image tasks. We support both CPU and GPU but if you have a large
collection of images it might take a while in the first time to embed all items if you are
not using a GPU.
Note
This is the first release of VectorVFS and we are expanding models and data types.
Currently we support only Perception Encoders (PE) and images.
Key Features
¶
Zero-overhead indexing
Embeddings are stored as extended attributes (xattrs) on each file, eliminating the need for external
index files or services.
Seamless retrieval
Perform searches across your filesystem, retrieving files by embedding similarity.
Flexible embedding support
Plug in any embedding model—from pre-trained transformers to custom feature extractors—and let
VectorVFS handle storage and lookup.
Lightweight and portable
Built on native Linux VFS functionality, VectorVFS requires no additional daemons, background
processes or databases.

data.author: stopachka
data.article_summary: Instant是一个结合Firebase和Supabase优点的实时数据库，支持关系同步，目标是成为像Figma、Notion等公司内部构建的技术。团队正在寻找一位创始TypeScript工程师，要求对类型工效有极致追求，能够提升开发者体验，并参与构建同步引擎。团队还注重UI设计，提升用户在CLI和Dashboard上的使用体验，包括改进迁移功能、沙盒和数据浏览器等。最终目标是通过精细的类型设计和用户友好的UI，打造一个让开发者享受使用的数据库。

43897138.article_content:
instant
instant
Founding Typescript Engineer
Instant is a real-time database you can use on the frontend. We give you the best of both Firebase and Supabase, a sync-engine with support for relations. This is the kind of tech that companies like Figma, Notion, and Linear build internally to power their products (
Try out the demo
)
We're looking for a founding Typescript Engineer to join our team of 4 in San Francisco. If you:
Are obsessive about type ergonomics (even with how types show up in intellisense)
Enjoy crafting UIs that people use for hours
Want to build a sync engine to enable the next Figma or Notion
Then we want to talk to you! So, why those three points? Let us explain:
1
.
You are obsessive about type ergonomics
One of the benefits about using typescript in a library is the developer experience you can offer your users. Types can do so much more than just catch typos. Types are a tool. They give you autocomplete and good feedback; shown in the right moment they can make someone's day. We don't just want to build a great database. We want people to enjoy using it.
Instant is
typed
. It took some serious
type fu
, but the upshot is the users get autocomplete and typesafety as a result. And right now types are a first cut. Here's some of what's ahead:
Type where clauses
Imagine you are building a goodreads alternative. You want to write a query like:
Give me profiles that have "Count of Monte Cristo" in their bookshelves
. This is how it would look in Instant:
{
profiles
:
{
$
:
{
where
:
{
"bookshelves.books.title"
:
"Count of Monte Cristo"
}
}
,
}
}
;
And with it you'd get those profiles. But
bookshelves.books.title
is typed too broadly: any string is allowed. This means users could have typos, or forget which relationships exist on
profiles
.
Well, we already have access to the schema. We
could
type the where clause. This way, when a user starts writing "booksh", we could autocomplete with all the relationships that live on
profiles
!
This is tricky (there's
a lot
you can do in a query), but it would be a huge benefit to users.
Improve intellisense
Or speaking of
schemas
: this is what you'll see in Typescript when you hover over one:

schema
:

<

<

>
;

...

...
